Digital sovereignty is a hot topic not only for governments but also for organisations that operate across jurisdictional and national boundaries - and therefore all major financial businesses.  Restricting the ability of foreign-owned or foreign-controlled organisations OR GOVERNMENTS to access data owned by, about or important to national citizens or interests and reducing dependence on foreign-owned or -controlled infrastructure is complex, but becoming a firm requirement from regulators and lawmakers.

Most approaches attempt to move computing resources - often to less-appropriate or favourable locations - or to rely on contractual agreements.

This session introduces an alternative: using Confidential Computing - a set of widely-available, hardware-based technologies - to isolate applications and their data from the underlying infrastructure, operators and owners, implementing a truly isolated zero-trust friendly architecture.  We will discuss the basics of the technology and then examine how well it fits the needs of digital sovereignty, explaining its applicability for use cases from finance, AI, Web3 and the broader Enterprise.

speakers.name: Mike Bursell
speakers.bio:
﻿Mike Bursell is the Executive Director of the Confidential Computing Consortium. He is one of the co-founders of the Enarx project (https://enarx.dev), and was CEO and co-founder of Profian, a start-up based on Enarx.  He has previously served on the Governing Boards of the CCC and the Bytecode Alliance and currently holds advisory board roles with various start-ups.  Previous companies include Red Hat, Intel and Citrix, with roles in security, virtualisation and networking.

Mike is author of "Trust in Computer Systems and the Cloud", published by Wiley in 2021.

talks.title: Under the Hood of Building on Lovable
talks.description: Fabian Hedin co-founded Lovable to turn intent into working software. As CTO, he shares what happens under the hood of the platform millions build on — and shows how Lovable became the engine for building powerful software that your own tools and AI agents can operate and build with. A keynote about the next era of how software gets built, shipped, and run.

speakers.name: Fabian Hedin
speakers.bio: Fabian Hedin is an accomplished entrepreneur and technology leader with a diverse background in founding and leading innovative companies—including serving as Co-Founder and CTO of Lovable, Founder and CEO of Tentium, and Founder and CTO of TenFAST. His earlier experience includes roles as Frontend Lead at Depict and Fullstack Engineer at CurbFood.

talks.title: The Signal Layer: What to Build When Anything Can Be Built
talks.description:
AI has made implementation faster, cheaper, and more widely available. That changes the real bottleneck in software.

Every team can generate code and spin up agents. The advantage moves to a different layer: knowing what is worth building, who it is for, how people will discover it, and how the product should behave once they do.

This keynote introduces the system of public signal, user intent, agent experience, distribution loops, and product judgment that helps builders decide what deserves to exist before they commit time, infrastructure, and trust to building it.

We will look at how AI changes the software lifecycle from “can we build it?” to “should this exist? When anything can be built, the most valuable builders are the ones who can read signal early and shape the right experience.

speakers.name: Lena Hall
speakers.bio: Lena Hall is an expert in practical AI adoption, data engineering, cloud and pragmatic architecture, driving strategic AI integration at scale combined with extensive experience leading large, high-performing technical teams. She is the Founder and CEO of Droid AI, where she helps businesses get real results from AI, defining Data +  AI strategies, integrating LLMs into complex systems, connecting AI solutions with custom data and business tools, and optimizing outcomes through proven and innovative architectures. Lena has 15+ years of deeply technical background as a solution architect, technical leader in large-scale data, analytics, machine learning, and cloud computing. Prior to Droid AI, Lena worked as Head of Developer Experience, North America at Amazon Web Services and led Big Data DevRel at Microsoft. She frequently shares practical knowledge on her YouTube channel (youtube.com/@lena-hall) and at industry conferences as an international keynote speaker.

talks.title: Fireside Chat - Why the future is built on “AND”
talks.description:
From AI to hybrid work to organizational culture, the most important breakthroughs happen when we stop thinking in opposites.
The tech industry loves binaries. Remote OR office. Build OR buy. AI replaces humans, OR AI empowers humans.
And social media makes it even worse,  because nuance doesn’t trend very well.
But maybe the future belongs to people who can think in terms of combinations rather than opposites. So today is really about one question:
How do we move from ‘either/or’ to ‘and’, as leaders, developers, organizations, and society?

speakers.name: Jürgen Hartwig
speakers.bio:
Jürgen Hartwig has been a member of the Board of Management of Daimler Truck Holding AG since December 2021 and is responsible for the Human Resources division.

Since June 2022, he has also served as Labor Director of Daimler Truck Holding AG, and since 2019 he has been a member of the Board of Management and Labor Director of Daimler Truck AG.

Before taking over the leadership of the Human Resources department for Daimler Trucks within Daimler AG, Jürgen Hartwig spent three years in Beijing as Director Human Resources Greater China. Prior to that, he held various positions in the areas of Human Resources, Corporate Organization & Change Management, as well as Process
Consulting & Organization.

He began his professional career in 1993 at the former Daimler-Benz AG in Gaggenau in the field of Human Resources & Organizational Development, after completing his studies in Business Education at the University of Mannheim.

speakers.name: Rudi Bauer
speakers.bio: That’s me

talks.title: Spot, Squash, Secure: Fighting Security Bugs with GitHub Copilot
talks.description: It's summer, and the bugs are biting — in your code and in your backyard. In this session, we'll take GitHub Copilot and GitHub Advanced Security for a spin to see how far AI-driven security has come, what it can actually catch, and where it still needs a swat. Come for the puns, stay for the demos.

speakers.name: Malte Lantin
speakers.bio: Malte Lantin is a Strategic Solutions Engineer at GitHub, where he helps large enterprises adopt modern software engineering practices, AI-powered developer workflows, and platform engineering at scale. Malte is based in Germany and brings more than 15 years of experience spanning software development, technical evangelism, program management, and solutions engineering. He is also the co-host of the German software engineering podcast TodoCast, where he discusses developer productivity, emerging technologies, and industry trends.

speakers.name: Marie Theresa Brosig
speakers.bio:
Marie Theresa has spent the past decade helping developers thrive by bridging the gap between technology and people — drawing on her background in both education and computer science.

She has a proven track record of making complex tools feel usable and human, and now works with some of the largest enterprise customers in EMEA to make AI a true peer programmer: one that supports developers everywhere.

Marie once helped run a cybersecurity book club, believes good documentation is a form of kindness, and rarely leaves the house without a paperback (or two) in tow.

talks.title: The Hidden Costs of CPU Limits in Kubernetes
talks.description:
CPU limits in Kubernetes are widely recommended as a best practice—but in real production systems they often introduce performance problems that are hard to observe, explain, or debug.

In this talk, we explore what actually happens inside the Linux kernel when CPU limits are enforced via cgroups, and how this impacts modern application runtimes. We’ll examine how CPU throttling interacts with the Linux scheduler, increases context switching, and restricts runnable threads in ways that are invisible at the Kubernetes abstraction layer.

A key focus of the session is how different runtimes manage their own concurrency. We’ll show that the number of runnable threads is not always fixed and can often be influenced, sometimes directly, sometimes indirectly, through runtime configuration and scheduling behavior. Using examples from Go, the JVM, and native C/C++ applications, we’ll demonstrate how aligning runtime-level concurrency with actual CPU availability can significantly reduce throttling and improve stability.

We’ll connect these mechanisms to real-world symptoms such as increased tail latency, unstable throughput, misleading autoscaling signals, and confusing observability data. The session concludes with practical guidance for DevOps and platform engineers on when CPU limits help, when they hurt, and how to design Kubernetes workloads that balance isolation, performance, and predictability.

speakers.name: Pavel Malyarevsky
speakers.bio:
Pavel Malyarevsky is an engineering leader and infrastructure practitioner with nearly 20 years of experience running large-scale, mission-critical systems. He is currently the Engineering Owner of the Container as a Service part of Private Cloud at Deutsche Bank in Berlin, where he designs and operates Kubernetes-based platforms supporting latency-sensitive and high-throughput workloads.

Pavel has led cloud and infrastructure organizations across multiple countries, managing fleets of tens of thousands of servers and network devices in highly regulated environments. His background spans Linux internals, distributed systems, observability, and production engineering, with a strong focus on performance and operational correctness.

Having worked extensively with containerized runtimes in real production environments, Pavel focuses on closing the gap between Kubernetes abstractions and the underlying behavior of the Linux kernel and application runtimes—especially where hidden performance costs emerge.

talks.title: Inside Mercedes-Benz: 140 Years of Heritage meet AI
talks.description:
How do you turn AI into real enterprise value—beyond pilots and hype?

Mercedes-Benz shares lessons from operating AI at scale: across legacy systems, compliance constraints, and complex organizations. The key insight: tools don’t make you AI-native—architecture, culture, and leadership do.

speakers.name: Daniel Geisel
speakers.bio:
Daniel Geisel is CEO of Mercedes‑Benz Tech Innovation. In this role, he is responsible for the global software organization within Mercedes‑Benz IT, driving technological development and innovation in close collaboration with the business functions.

Under his leadership, the organization is evolving from individual tech hubs into a globally integrated software tech organization, combining software engineering excellence, digital solutions and strong execution capabilities. He works closely with international teams across locations including Spain, South Africa, India and Malaysia.

speakers.name: Jens Petersohn
speakers.bio:
Jens is CTO of Mercedes-Benz Tech Innovation. His journey into tech began around 2006: debugging Internet Explorer 6, writing PHP that would make any modern linter weep, and genuinely believing that document.all was a reasonable API. Somehow, that did not scare him off.

He joined Mercedes-Benz as a software engineer in 2014, and by 2017 had taken on additional responsibility as Principal for Connected Vehicle Services, shaping how cars talk to the cloud and, occasionally, back. Since 2023, he serves as CTO, driving innovation, embedding AI across the product development lifecycle, and steering a 7,500-person engineering organization at the heart of Mercedes-Benz's global software ecosystem.

He still has opinions about JavaScript. They've just gotten harder to revert.

talks.title: Code Style in Practice: Balancing Preferences and Consistency
talks.description:
How often do we work with code where similar parts look different and are difficult to understand? The reasons are not always clear and are often related to personal preferences, missing standards, or historical decisions.

In this talk, we will discuss:
Is it better to follow an exciting coding style rather than introduce your own?
When and how is it appropriate to improve or change code style?
Can principles be used when formal standards do not exist?
How do code style and consistency impact readability, maintainability, and overall code quality?

This talk focuses on balancing personal preferences with shared team consistency and on making software projects easier and more enjoyable to work with.

speakers.name: Angelika Shvets
speakers.bio:
Angelika Shvets, a software developer based in Israel.
I've been in the IT industry since 2004.
Over the last 7 years, my work has primarily involved software development, encompassing research, implementation, integration, and testing of systems of varying complexity.
Prior to my current role, I spent 8 years as a full-stack web application developer.
In the early stages of my career, I gained a solid foundation with 5 years of experience as a system administrator.
I also served as a system administrator in the military.
I hold a Masters in Mathematics and Computer Engineering.

talks.title: The Future of Knowledge Retention: AI-Driven HR Transformation
talks.description:
We show how AI and intelligent automation can be used as a digital mentor and efficiency driver to significantly relieve HR burdens while systematically preserving experiential knowledge within the company for the next generation.

HR work is currently at a historic turning point. More than 50 percent of HR time is spent on administrative tasks, while a massive loss of knowledge looms by 2035 as a large share of operational specialists retire.

speakers.name: Trecilla Lobo
speakers.bio: As SVP, People & Culture at Flip, Trecilla Lobo specializes in building workplace cultures that drive high performance. She brings over two decades of expertise in scaling global tech firms and is responsible for Flip’s end-to-end people strategy, ensuring that inclusivity and engagement remain at the heart of the company’s growth.

talks.title: Beyond the Wrapper: Technical Bets That VCs Back
talks.description: Substance over hype. While the tech world chases shiny interfaces, the real value is being built deep in the stack. What separates a short-lived "wrapper" from sustainable, long-term tech infrastructure? This panel goes past the marketing noise to analyze the core technological bets capturing strategic venture capital right now.

speakers.name: Christian Nagel
speakers.bio:
Filip is a Founding Partner at Cherry. Originally on track to become a classically trained musician, he took an unexpected detour into entrepreneurship — and never looked back.

Before becoming an investor, Filip built and scaled multiple ventures. He first founded a digital marketplace for art and collectibles, then joined the founding team of Zalando, where he focused on product, business development, and international expansion. His work helped turn Zalando into Europe’s leading lifestyle destination. These experiences gave him a deep understanding of the founder journey — the challenges, the breakthroughs, and the constant need to build — and shape his hands-on approach to supporting Cherry’s portfolio companies.

Beyond Cherry, Filip serves on the board of KfW Capital, the German Startup Association, and the Board of Trustees of the State Opera Berlin. He guest lectures at WHU and IMD Lausanne, and through his family foundation, works to provide access to entrepreneurship and education for underprivileged families.

Filip is a three-time Midas List Europe honoree and was named Investor of the Year 2022 by the German Startup Association.

He is especially drawn to founders pushing the frontier of technology — from AI to deep tech and breakthrough products. Filip partners with visionary teams like The Exploration Company, robeauté, and Proxima Fusion to help turn bold ideas into the next generation of category-defining companies.

speakers.name: Filip Dames
speakers.bio:
Filip is a Founding Partner at Cherry. Originally on track to become a classically trained musician, he took an unexpected detour into entrepreneurship — and never looked back.

Before becoming an investor, Filip built and scaled multiple ventures. He first founded a digital marketplace for art and collectibles, then joined the founding team of Zalando, where he focused on product, business development, and international expansion. His work helped turn Zalando into Europe’s leading lifestyle destination. These experiences gave him a deep understanding of the founder journey — the challenges, the breakthroughs, and the constant need to build — and shape his hands-on approach to supporting Cherry’s portfolio companies.

Beyond Cherry, Filip serves on the board of KfW Capital, the German Startup Association, and the Board of Trustees of the State Opera Berlin. He guest lectures at WHU and IMD Lausanne, and through his family foundation, works to provide access to entrepreneurship and education for underprivileged families.

Filip is a three-time Midas List Europe honoree and was named Investor of the Year 2022 by the German Startup Association.

He is especially drawn to founders pushing the frontier of technology — from AI to deep tech and breakthrough products. Filip partners with visionary teams like The Exploration Company, robeauté, and Proxima Fusion to help turn bold ideas into the next generation of category-defining companies.

speakers.name: Justus Lumpe
speakers.bio:
Justus is Co-CEO at i5invest. During his career he has built a strong network with international corporates, successful entrepreneurs and start-ups as well as leading investors.
Through leveraging market and industry experience Justus helps tech companies define their strategy, gain market traction, scale and exit internationally.
Justus started his career as a consultant at PwC and Capco. Following his MBA he joined Lehman Brothers as an investment banker in London, covering European Industrials. He then worked for Nomura and RBC, where he helped to build the European Industrials investment banking practice. He advised on numerous buyside and sellside transactions, financings and initial public offerings, mainly focusing on capital goods and automotive space.
Justus also was a Managing Director at NOAH, a boutique corporate finance advisory firm. At NOAH he ran the partnership business focused on NOAH Conference, the leading events for the European digital ecosystem.
Justus studied Business Administration in Germany and England, and holds an MBA with high distinction from the Tuck School of Business.

speakers.name: Philipp Moehring
speakers.bio:
Philipp Moehring is the founder and Managing Partner of Tiny, one of Europe's top-performing pre-seed venture firms. Before Tiny, Philipp spent four years at Seedcamp, then seven years at AngelList where he launched and ran the European business. Through that time, he saw first-hand what works and what breaks at the earliest stage of company building — and what most investors get wrong.

He cofounded Tiny to back the best technical founders in Europe at the moment they need it most: before anyone else is paying attention. The results have been consistent, and Tiny is now one of the best pre seed funds in Europe. Tiny backed nine unicorns including n8n, Wayve, Synthesia, and Payhawk from their first rounds.

talks.title: Building Accountability in Agentic AI
talks.description: Current infrastructural speed has outpaced accountability as AI agents increasingly become autonomous decision makers across organisations. When an agentic decision is made, how do we verify the rationale behind it, and where does the audit trail start when things go wrong? This session will explore the vital intersection of hyper-scale AI platforms and decentralised systems, shedding light on why immutable public ledgers can be the missing piece for enterprise AI governance.

speakers.name: Frederik Gregaard
speakers.bio: As CEO of the Cardano Foundation, Frederik Gregaard brings over two decades of leadership experience, including his tenure at PwC, where he spearheaded transformative initiatives in digital innovation. Under his guidance, the Foundation has become a catalyst for blockchain adoption, driving impactful solutions in decentralized governance and sustainability. Frederik’s leadership emphasizes transparency, regulatory alignment, and fostering global collaboration to build a more inclusive and decentralized future.

speakers.name: Mariana de la Roche W.
speakers.bio: Mariana de la Roche Wills is an international lawyer and founder of BlackVogel and DAAvern, advising institutions, regulators, and Web3 companies on digital assets, DAOs, and trusted data infrastructure. She translates policy into implementation, designing technology-ethical and compliance frameworks, compliance-by-design roadmaps, and cross-border adoption plans. Mariana convenes expert roundtables globally, bringing together industry leaders and authorities to advance regulatory clarity and institutional adoption. Her focus spans MiCA, AML/CFT, DAO governance, digital identity, and AI×Web3 convergence across the global level with particular focus on Europe and Latin America.

talks.title: Software Engineering for Muggles
talks.description:
Have you ever tried to explain software engineering to someone who’s never written a line of code? It’s surprisingly hard, because unlike building a house, software projects rarely go according to plan. They end up more like… the Weasley house from Harry Potter.

What starts as a simple, sturdy home becomes an ever-expanding, slightly chaotic structure of extensions, workarounds, last-minute rooms, and “temporary” solutions that somehow end up permanent. Software engineering isn't about a single big construction project, it's an ongoing journey of planning, building, testing, and fixing. Using the Weasley house as a metaphor, I’ll explain why we’re always “renovating” (maintenance), why swapping out doors (libraries) means checking the versions of the hinges and door frames, and how, in software, we can simply “copy the whole house” to test new windows — without anyone catching a cold.

After this session you will never struggle again explaining software engineering concepts to your mum, your non technical friend, or your nephew again. Give it a try!

speakers.name: Theresa Heine
speakers.bio: Theresa Heine is a Product Owner with a software engineering background, focused on software quality, test automation, and release processes. Passionate about improving reliability in legacy systems while adapting quality practices for AI-driven development. Known for making complex technical topics understandable and bridging the gap between technical and non-technical stakeholders.

talks.title: AI in Recruiting: What Works, What Fails - Real Lessons from Office & Volume Hiring
talks.description:
AI has huge potential in recruiting - but implementations vary widely. This talk breaks down what worked, what didn’t, and why, across both office (professional) and volume (high-velocity) hiring environments.
In this practical session, you’ll hear real, data-backed lessons from multiple AI introductions we led at Redcare Pharmacy and evaluated in both office hiring and volume recruiting.

I’ll cover:
- Successful patterns - where AI improved work of the recruiters / candidate experience.
- Unsuccessful rollouts - where tools underperformed and what were the reasons.
- Human + machine workflows - what roles remain human-centric, and where AI delivers the most leverage.
- Ethics and bias safeguards - real examples of how bias surfaced, and practical guardrails to address it.
- Metrics that matter -  what to measure when you deploy AI so you know you’re improving, not guessing.

speakers.name: Barbara Kryslak
speakers.bio: Barbara Kryslak is a talent leader with extensive experience in both strategic recruiting and the operational deployment of HR technologies. She has led cross-functional teams through AI adoption initiatives, driving measurable improvements in hiring quality and operational efficiency across diverse talent markets.

talks.title: 200 OK: Payment settled, resource delivered
talks.description: AI agents are making machine-to-machine payments on the open web in the rapidly growing field of agentic commerce. We’ll explore next-generation payment protocols, open web standards, and blockchain solutions that enable digital payments in the burgeoning agentic economy. Learn about recent developments, technical challenges, and emerging standards that are shaping how agents exchange value at internet scale.

speakers.name: Brian Whippo
speakers.bio: Brian is the Senior Director of Integrations and Developer Tools at Algorand Foundation, where he helps devs learn, integrate, and contribute to Algorand's open source blockchain technology to solve real world problems. Before joining the Foundation, Brian led global strategic transformation programs at Morgan Stanley, where he led technology change programs for commodities, exchange-traded and OTC derivatives, Prime Brokerage, and digital assets businesses over 15 years. When not on his laptop, he's probably cooking slow food that makes the house smell good.

talks.title: TypeScript Features That Changed the Game
talks.description:
TypeScript emerged as a practical, editor-first extension of JavaScript to help teams scale JavaScript with a structural, gradual type system and better tooling.

This talk traces that origin story and highlights the features that "changed the game" from strict null checking and discriminated unions to advanced conditional/template literal types and recent compiler performance advances.

speakers.name: Dani Coll
speakers.bio: Dani began his tech journey at a startup 10 years ago as a mobile developer. Over the years, he worked at several consulting companies, gaining some experience across multiple stacks. Eventually, he specialized in frontend development and is now focused on advocating for the field by writing technical content, conducting workshops and giving talks.

talks.title: Programming with Contracts in C++26
talks.description: C++26 adds contracts, a construct known from Design-by-Contract. In this session we will take a practical look at what they are, how to use them, what they can do now, and what lies in its near and far future.

speakers.name: Peter Bindels
speakers.bio: Peter is an experienced C++ software developer with a particular interest in making things simpler. Part of making things simpler is to understand the full complexity of a particular problem and then seeing what the simplest solution that is still sufficient would be. He is a part of the ISO C++ Committee since 2019 and participates mostly in the Tooling (SG15), Unicode (SG16), Contracts (SG21) and Safety (SG23) study groups.

talks.title: Nemotron: NVIDIA's open model strategy for developers
talks.description: In this session, we take a focused, developer-first look at the NVIDIA Nemotron model family. We'll walk through the architecture behind Nemotron, how these models are pre-trained at scale, and the end-to-end fine-tuning workflow using NVIDIA NeMo. From customizing models with your own data to deploying them efficiently in production, this talk covers the practical steps developers need to get started with Nemotron today. Whether you're building enterprise copilots, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, or domain-specific language applications, you'll leave with a clear understanding of how to leverage these open models in your own stack.

speakers.name: Sergio Perez
speakers.bio: Sergio Perez specializes in conversational AI. He has experience in optimizing training and inference of LLMs, building retrieval-augmented generation systems, and working with companies in different sectors to leverage AI. His area of expertise at NVIDIA is quantization and inference serving. Previously, he worked as an AI engineer at Graphcore and Amazon, and got a Ph.D. in computational fluid dynamics from Imperial College London.

talks.title: Synthetic Insiders: The New AI Risk to Your Org
talks.description: What happens when the attacker isn’t malware, but a “colleague”? AI is enabling scammers to deploy synthetic identities that can pass interviews with stolen identities, integrate into teams, and access internal systems at scale. In this talk, we unpack how deepfakes, LLM agents, and automation are reshaping the threat landscape, using real cases, underground techniques, and a live demo to show why trust has become the most exploited layer in modern IT architectures.

speakers.name: George Proorocu
speakers.bio:
George is a seasoned IT professional with 15+ years of experience, evolving from technical roles to leading engineering teams in security-critical sectors. Passionate about coaching and empowering others, he combines hands-on expertise with strategic leadership.

A former professional chess player, George won the "Romanian Chess Champion" title with his club team in 2004. At 16, he founded and grew an ISP company in Bucharest to 600 clients before selling it at 18. He later pursued an Executive MBA at IMT Paris to strengthen his leadership skills.

Recognized in the Financial Times' "100 Faces of Innovation" in 2016, George is a sought-after Cybersecurity expert specializing in Fraud and Deepfakes. He has spoken at over 20 conferences all around the world, and his beginner’s Cybersecurity course has helped 150,000+ students start their careers in the field.

talks.title: Go's Concurrency and Parallelism Inside Containers
talks.description:
A common assumption is that if a program is concurrent, it will also run in parallel, and that containers simply get a number of CPU cores to work with. In practice, neither of these assumptions holds.

In this talk we explore how concurrency and parallelism behave inside containers, and why the same program can show very different performance characteristics when run on the host versus inside a container with CPU limits applied.

Using a small Go program as an example, we start with a simple sequential implementation, introduce concurrency to structure the work, and then add parallelism to scale CPU bound processing. We observe how the program behaves under different container CPU configurations, and where expectations break down.

speakers.name: Rick Rackow
speakers.bio: Rick Rackow is a seasoned professional in the IT industry with a strong background in cloud and container infrastructure. An SRE at heart, he has worked extensively with distributed systems, Linux, and Go, and focuses on building and operating reliable, observable systems in real world production environments.

talks.title: Creating Europe's AI Moment – Now or Never
talks.description: Europe has the talent, the research and the industry, but turning that into global AI leadership is another matter. This panel brings industry and policy to the same table to ask what it would really take for Europe to lead rather than follow. An honest look at where Europe stands and what has to change.

speakers.name: Antonella Mei-Pochtler
speakers.bio:
Antonella is an Italian executive and multiple board member with many years of strategy consulting experience at BCG, where she became one of the youngest partners and a member of its global executive committee. Her work focus is in media, technology, and consumer goods. She was named amongst the top 25 consultants worldwide by Consulting Magazine and was honored with the Women Leaders in Consulting Lifetime Achievement Award in 2013.

From 2018 to 2022, she was Special Advisor to the Austrian Chancellor and headed the ThinkAustria strategy unit. She also co-chaired the Kofi Annan Award for Innovation in Africa.

Today, she is CEO of iSi Group, Executive Vice Chairwoman of Pochtler Industrieholding and contributes her in-depth transformation expertise as non-executive director in international supervisory boards (Generali, Publicis, Westwing, and DEAG). Previously, amongst other positions, she was Chairwoman of the Supervisory Board of Wolford and an IFC-nominated director at the Ivorian company SIPRA.

She is strongly engaged in the non-profit sector, among others as a Vice-President of the European Forum Alpbach (EFA) and co-founder of the Sovereign Europe Forum, board member at TUM Venture Labs and advisory board member of the Drucker Forum. She has been committed to equal opportunities in education for many years (Teach For All, Business@School, Phorms Schools) and has published essays on leadership and strategy (“Acupuncture for Management”).

Antonella studied in Munich and Rome and has an MBA with distinction from INSEAD. She lives with her family in Vienna.

speakers.name: Thomas Jarzombek
speakers.position: Parliamentary State Secretary to the Federal Minister for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation
speakers.bio:
Thomas Jarzombek was born in Düsseldorf and has been active in politics for more than 25 years. He served as a member of the Düsseldorf City Council and as a member of the State Parliament of North Rhine-Westphalia.

Since 2009, he has been a Member of the German Bundestag.

From 2013 to 2018, he acted as the spokesperson for the Digital Agenda of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group. Between 2018 and 2021, Thomas Jarzombek served as the Federal Government Coordinator for Aerospace, and from 2019 to 2021, as the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs’ Representative for the Digital Economy and Start-ups.

Most recently, from 2021 to 2025, he was the spokesperson for Education and Research of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group and a member of the Committee on Digital Affairs. Since May 2025, he has served as Parliamentary State Secretary to the Federal Minister for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation.

speakers.name: Thomas Saueressig
speakers.position: CCO and Member of the Executive Board
speakers.bio:
Thomas Saueressig is a Member of the Executive Board and Chief Customer Officer of SAP SE.

His board area, the Customer Value Group (CVG), brings together SAP’s go-to-market and delivery functions to help customers effectively drive their business transformation, fully leverage the benefits of AI, and build long-term customer value in the cloud.

Saueressig has a strong track record of delivering customer value. In his previous role, he led the Executive Board area Customer Services & Delivery, where he worked closely with customers to achieve business outcomes through innovation and end-to-end business transformation.

Before being appointed the head of SAP Product Engineering, Saueressig served as Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Global Head of IT Services at SAP. As CIO, he was responsible for SAP’s IT strategy and its execution with a cloud-first approach. Saueressig joined SAP in 2004 in consulting and subsequently held various international management positions with increasing responsibility.

Saueressig holds a degree in Business Informatics from the Baden-Wuerttemberg Cooperative State University in Mannheim and a joint Executive MBA from ESSEC Business School (France) and Mannheim Business School (Germany).

Since April 2022, he has been a member of the Board of Directors of Nokia and serves as vice-chairman.

speakers.name: Jasper Bennink
speakers.bio: As a reporter for the POLITICO Technology & AI newsletter, I am following every tech- and AI-related in both Berlin and Brussels closely. I’m mostly passionate about how AI development and implementation become increasingly geopolitical issues.

talks.title: Small, Secure, Interconnected: The next Internet Protocol
talks.description: We keep building giant, centralized “one network to rule them all,” then spend years bolting on access controls, tickets, and spreadsheets. There’s an easier way: build small, human‑sized private networks that interconnect safely when you need them to. This talk shows how identity‑based networking, least‑privilege defaults, and explicit, auditable sharing let teams collaborate across companies without hair‑pin VPNs or six‑month firewall adventures. We’ll cover practical design patterns (identity as the perimeter; tags and groups, not subnets), the sharp edges you’ll hit (contractors, labs, and ghost machines), and a simple approach to cross‑organization access that you can explain to both auditors and developers. The goal is to make secure access boringly reliable and easy to revoke—so the fastest path is the secure path.

speakers.name: Ross Kukulinski
speakers.bio:
Ross Kukulinski is Vice President of Product at Tailscale, where he leads product strategy and execution across the company's secure connectivity platform.

Ross is a technical product leader who builds businesses at the intersection of open source, cloud infrastructure, and developer experience. He has spent nearly two decades working on cloud-native technologies, helping organizations move from early adoption to reliable, large-scale production use. His work has focused on turning complex distributed systems into products that are easier to adopt, operate, and trust—without hiding the underlying engineering or limiting flexibility.

Before joining Tailscale, Ross was VP of Product Management at Kong, where he led the transformation from packaged on-prem software to a cloud-first platform. Prior to Kong, he spent four years at VMware following the acquisition of Heptio, where he was an initial employee. At Heptio and VMware, he led product for Kubernetes platforms including Tanzu Kubernetes Grid, working closely with engineering teams and customers to shape how modern infrastructure is packaged, delivered, and operated.

Ross is passionate about building products that balance strong technical foundations with clear customer value, mentoring future product leaders, and earning developer trust through great experiences.

talks.title: The 8th Layer: Building the Open AI Stack Before It Builds You
talks.description:
We’ve spent decades perfecting the software stack — from LAMP to cloud-native to platform engineering. But AI is reshaping that stack in real time.

The real risk isn’t just technical debt. It’s strategic dependency.

In this lightning talk, Raffi Krikorian explores “the 8th layer” of the AI stack — the layer beyond infrastructure, models, and APIs — where incentives, governance, and control determine who actually benefits from AI.

What would a true “LAMP Stack for AI” look like? One that is open, composable, inspectable, and community-governed. One where developers aren’t just API consumers but builders of durable systems.

We’ll break down the emerging Open AI stack — from data to models to orchestration — and why openness at each layer matters for security, sovereignty, and long-term innovation.

If you’re building with AI, you’re already choosing a stack.

The question is: are you building it — or renting it?

speakers.name: Raffi Krikorian
speakers.bio:
Raffi Krikorian is Chief Technology Officer at Mozilla, where he leads efforts to build trustworthy technology that serves the public interest and strengthens human agency. A long-time member of the Mozilla community - serving on the Mozilla Foundation Board since 2023, Mozilla.ai’s Board since 2024, and the Mozilla.org Board since its inception - Raffi brings a record of impact across technology, politics, media, and philanthropy.

He previously served as CTO of Emerson Collective, where he focused on how technology and data can be used to drive solutions that promote social good; as the first CTO of the Democratic National Committee, where he built the technology, data, and security infrastructure that supported Democratic candidates nationwide; as Director of Uber’s Advanced Technologies Center, where he led the rollout of the first passenger-carrying self-driving car fleet; and as Vice President of Platform Engineering at Twitter, where he designed and scaled the systems that powered Twitter’s global platform.

He also created Technically Optimistic - a podcast and Substack exploring technology’s impact on society - which during its run reached #2 on Apple’s tech podcast charts and featured conversations with leaders including Sal Khan, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Ressa, Cory Doctorow, and Congressman Jay Obernolte.

talks.title: Smaller Voice Models
talks.description: In this talk, we’ll cover why some tasks only need smaller models: benefiting from zero cost, privacy, low latency, and offline reliability. Using voice AI as the example, we’ll explore how compact text-to-speech models can run on-device or on-premise, avoiding the cost and latency of cloud-only systems. We’ll share practical lessons from building smaller voice models, where they work well, where larger models are still useful, and how developers can think about model size as a product decision rather than just a benchmark. The session is aimed at anyone building real-time AI applications, voice agents, embedded tools, or privacy-sensitive user experiences.

speakers.name: Sohaib Ahmad
speakers.bio: Sohaib Ahmad is the CEO of Neuphonic, a London-based voice AI company building fast, compact text-to-speech models for real-time applications. He leads Neuphonic’s work on making voice AI more responsive, private, and deployable across cloud, on-device, and on-premise environments. With a background in Speech & Machine Learning from Cambridge University, and 10 years as a Quant Trader, Sohaib brings a practical perspective on building efficient AI systems that work in the real-world.

talks.title: Type Systems You Might Not Know (But Will Love)
talks.description:
Most devs, when confronted with types, only have to worry about "static vs dynamic". In this talk, we will demystify all those languages you’ve heard about for their weird type systems (Haskell, anyone?) as well as talk about type systems you might never have heard of, and discover why they’re awesome, useful, and solve real bugs! We’ll start with Rust’s affine ownership and Agda’s dependent types before touring a few out-there ideas.

We’ll build a solid mental model for modern production type systems as well as build a foundation for you to dive deeper into more obscure type system research if you so desire. We’ll build tiny runnable models, explore implementations, and you’ll leave with frameworks, resources, and a roadmap to go deeper, without needing a PhD.

speakers.name: Veit Heller
speakers.bio: I’m a technologist at heart, though life often leads me into managerial roles. For the last 15 years, I’ve built products, led and advised companies, published papers, and shared my insights at conferences and in articles on the web.

talks.title: Building the Nervous System of AI
talks.description: Michael Kagan, NVIDIA’s CTO, explains how AI factories are scaling toward million-GPU data centers, what drove NVIDIA’s evolution from a chip company into an AI infrastructure company, and why networking has become the “nervous system” of AI.

speakers.name: Michael Kagan
speakers.bio:
Michael Kagan serves as a Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of NVIDIA since May 2020, following the company’s acquisition of Mellanox Technologies, the company which he co-founded.

With over 40 years in the tech industry, Michael’s career began at Intel, where he contributed to 80387 math co-processor design, led 8060XP processor architecture and managed Pentium MMX design team. At Mellanox he played a pivotal role in developing accelerated networking technologies that enhanced cloud data center efficiency.

Today, as Nvidia’s CTO, Michael is focused on architecting solutions for evolving demands of artificial intelligence, developing architecture of data center as a single unit of computing – the AI factory. Michael focuses on full-stack solution, emphasizing importance of software in conjunction with hardware, advocating for the future where AI computing is accessible across diverse platforms from mega-scale data centers to mobile devices.

talks.title: Life Cycle Impact Assessment in TypeScript
talks.description:
Life cycle assessment of hardware products is becoming more important, as sustainability is a thing. The common tool "OpenLCA" is designed for expert use - but there is a TypeScript API. It allows you to write a simple UI and automate calculations of life cycle assessments.
In this live session I present a simplified LCA study first in OpenLCA, then write a React frontend with the "olca-ipc" TypeScript library and perform the same calculation in a web browser.

speakers.name: Corinna John
speakers.bio: Corinna lives in Hannover and works in renewable energies, always trying to connect coding with sustainability ideas. She ues C# since the year 2002 and has recently jumped into TypeScript for an LCIA project.

talks.title: The AI-Fluent Team: A Playbook for Driving Enterprise AI Transformation
talks.description:
Enterprises have poured billions into AI, across models, tools, and budgets, but most have almost nothing to show for it at scale. Individuals may be using AI to streamline their own workflows, but widespread adoption at the team level remains elusive. The reason? Most organizations still haven't cracked how to measure AI's effectiveness across an entire enterprise. The missing piece isn’t better technology, it’s a measurement and adoption framework that works at the team level, not just the individual level.

Avani Prabhakar, Atlassian's Chief People and AI Enablement Officer, owns both workforce strategy and AI transformation. In this session, Avani will share Atlassian's newly launched playbook for enterprise AI adoption, including data from her Teamwork Lab, and the following takeaways:

The #1 mistake organizations make when assessing AI's impact on their workforce

How People leaders are best-placed to strategically integrate AI into culture and practice

Why you must start with trapped knowledge (the expertise locked in your teams' heads), not technology

How Atlassian is measuring the return on investment from AI

This session is designed for enterprise AI leaders who are looking for a practical way to measure AI's effectiveness and a repeatable framework with proven ROI, told from the perspective of a leader who has driven it from the inside.

speakers.name: Avani Prabhakar
speakers.position: Chief People  and AI Enablement Officer
speakers.bio:
Atlassian Chief People and AI Enablement Officer, Avani Prabhakar, leads Atlassian's People and Transformations organisation with a sharp focus on unlocking potential in the AI era – blending purpose, systems thinking, and modern leadership to shape the future of work.

Avani’s focus is on enabling the cultural transformation required alongside the technology shift – to build AI-fluent teams and unlock opportunity. She has been instrumental in pioneering the distributed work models and ways of working that underpin Atlassian’s Team Anywhere approach, and is actively embedding AI up-skilling, scaling, and innovation across the organisation.

With 20+ years across tech, aviation, engineering, professional services and consulting, Avani keeps Atlassian's people-first approach practical and grounded, to build human + AI collaboration and capability in complex, high-growth environments.

talks.title: RTX AI PC: Developing local and edge AI applications
talks.description: Introduction to developing AI applications that run locally on RTX-powered PCs — privacy-first, offline-capable, low-latency use cases. Covers NVIDIA NIM on-device, NemoClaw open agent stack, and developer workflow for local model deployment.

speakers.name: Joerg Krall
speakers.bio:
Joerg Krall is a Senior Industry Business Development Manager for Automotive EMEA at NVIDIA, where he drives business development and strategic partnerships across Europe’s automotive ecosystem. Based in Germany, Joerg works with leading OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, and technology partners to accelerate the adoption of NVIDIA’s automotive platforms — including NVIDIA DRIVE — across the region.

With deep expertise spanning enterprise GPU solutions, XR/visualisation, and autonomous vehicle technologies, Joerg brings a broad technical and commercial perspective to NVIDIA’s automotive go-to-market in EMEA. He is a regular speaker at industry events, having presented at forums such as the XR-Symposium at SRH Hochschule Heidelberg, and has worked extensively with enterprise and industrial customers across Germany and Europe.

Prior to his focus on automotive, Joerg held roles within NVIDIA’s Worldwide Field Operations supporting enterprise visualisation and vGPU deployments for customers including Thales, Atos, and science+computing ag.

talks.title: Building the next generation of AI developer tools
talks.description:
AI has already changed software development. Tools like GitHub Copilot have become ubiquitous part of the workflow of millions of developers. Like other well-known editor features, AI-in-editor increases productivity, reduces required context switching, and lets developers stay in the flow while focusing on important parts of their job.

However, this was just a first step - with the rapid developments of large language models (LLMs), which have become more powerful and knowledgeable with every release and have excellent reasoning capabilities, we can do more. Nowadays, we see AI agents such as Claude Code able to solve complex, repository-wide tasks or even generate whole applications.

In the talk, I will discuss how AI developer tools has changed over the years, describe emerging usage patterns of AI agents and how they change whole software development process, and peek into the future of developer tools. All that while trying to answer the most important question - how to design applications using AI with humans in mind.

speakers.name: Krzysztof Cieślak
speakers.bio:
Krzysztof is a photographer, globetrotter, and public speaker. He works as a Staff Research Engineer at [GitHub Next](https://next.github.com/), where he designs and builds the next generation of developer tools such as GitHub Copilot, NES or [REDACTED]

After the work, Krzysztof is an open-source software maintainer passionate about functional programming (especially F#), editor tooling and developer experience - he has created and maintained several OSS projects varying from [language servers](https://github.com/fsharp/FsAutoComplete) to [web frameworks](https://github.com/SaturnFramework/Saturn) to [VSCode plugins](https://github.com/ionide/ionide-vscode-fsharp).

Additionally, he is a passionate public speaker. You can meet him at many conferences around the world, where he is always trying to meet new people and learn how to improve software developers' lives.

talks.title: From AI Assistance to Agentic Systems: Scaling Sovereign AI in Banking
talks.description:
AI is no longer defined by experimentation, it is defined by expectations.
Customers expect intelligent guidance, employees expect real relief in their daily work, and regulators expect transparency, control, and accountability.
In this joint keynote, Julia Koch (Finanz Informatik) and Markus Hacker (NVIDIA) share how AI transformation evolves when it’s built for everyday impact, sovereign operation, and agentic capabilities at scale. Building one of the largest AI implementations worldwide in the financial sector, Julia shares insights from the transition from AI assistants to agentic AI systems that proactively support complex processes across highly regulated, large-scale ecosystems.
The session focuses on three decisive factors of effective AI transformation:
•	Use-case-driven value creation, ensuring AI delivers measurable benefits for customers and employees
•	agentic architectures, enabling AI systems to reason, orchestrate, and act within clearly defined boundaries
•	and sovereignty, providing full control over data, models, and infrastructure as a prerequisite for trust, compliance, and scalability.
Attendees will gain insights into how Finanz Informatik builds and operates a fully sovereign and 100% on-prem AI platform for the Savings Banks Finance Group, scaling AI assistance and agentic capabilities across 341 institutions, 200,000 employees and 50 million customers. NVIDIA complements this perspective by showing how accelerated computing and modern AI architectures enable sovereign AI factories to run reliably, efficiently, and sustainably at enterprise scale.
This session shows how AI becomes a growth engine when organizations move from pilots to platforms, from tools to systems, and from innovation promises to everyday impact.

speakers.name: Julia Koch
speakers.bio: As CTO and CCO, Julia Koch is responsible for the strategic direction and execution of software development, guiding her teams in delivering innovative and customer-centric banking solutions for the German Savings Banks Group, which serves over 50 million people in Germany. Her core objective is to lead her teams in shaping the future of modern banking. She’s committed to harnessing AI and other innovative technologies to enhance customer experience.

speakers.name: Markus Hacker
speakers.bio:
Markus leads the Enterprise Business for NVIDIA in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Based in Munich, he oversees the company’s go-to-market activities for enterprises in Central Europe, focusing on advancing AI, visualization, and virtualization technologies.
Markus’ career began in Microsoft’s Central European Data Centeroperations. Before joining NVIDIA in 2019, he held leadership roles at Akamai, Lionbridge, T-Systems, and Colt Technology Services. His two decades of experience in sales and business management have equipped him with deep expertise in the IT industry's evolving needs.
Markus is committed to fostering innovation and making valuable contributions to the field of AI. At NVIDIA, Markus leverages his knowledge to help businesses achieve their AI and industrial digitalization goals.

talks.title: From Static Rules to Reasoning Platforms: Scaling Intelligent Canary Delivery in 2026
talks.description:
As organizations scale their Kubernetes footprint, the "Day 2" reality of GitOps becomes clear: static thresholds are brittle. Standard Canary rollouts rely on fixed Prometheus queries (e.g., Error Rate < 1%), but these rules lack the context to distinguish between a minor transient blip and a systemic failure. For Platform Engineers, this results in "Alert Fatigue" and manual "promotion" gates that slow down the delivery pipeline.
In 2026, we are moving from Static Automation to Reasoning Platforms.
This session explores how to evolve your delivery infrastructure into an intelligent system that doesn't just follow rules, but reasons through data. We will demonstrate how to wrap ArgoCD Rollouts with an Agentic Reasoning Layer capable of cross-referencing metrics, logs, and distributed traces to make autonomous "Go/No-Go" decisions.

We will trigger a Canary deployment that passes basic health checks but introduces a "silent failure" (e.g., a cache hit-rate drop causing downstream latency). You will see the Reasoning Platform detect the anomaly, pause the rollout, "investigate" the root cause, and present a natural-language justification for the automated rollback.

speakers.name: Daniel Oh
speakers.bio: Daniel Oh is a Java Champion and Senior Principal Developer Advocate at IBM, where he leads efforts to advance cloud native innovation through open source technologies. Renowned for his ability to bridge technical and collaborative gaps, he empowers developers and organizations to build transformative solutions from AI-driven applications and serverless architectures to resilient microservices. As a CNCF Ambassador and TAG DevEx co-chair, Daniel actively shapes the cloud native ecosystem, fostering partnerships between enterprise developers, AI engineers, and platform engineering teams to accelerate hybrid cloud adoption. His technical leadership extends beyond code contributions, as he mentors communities and champions strategies that enable businesses to thrive in evolving digital landscapes. A dynamic storyteller and educator, Daniel captivates global audiences through keynote speeches, workshops, and interactive sessions, where he demystifies emerging technologies and inspires the tech community to embrace the future of open source innovation.

talks.title: Bulletproof Web Applications: The 2025 OWASP Top Ten
talks.description: Since 2003, the Open Web Application Security Project curates a list of the top ten security risks for web applications. The brand new 2025 edition of the OWASP Top Ten is on the horizon; time to take a look at it! What's new, what has changed, and what is mandatory knowledge for any developer using a modern web stack? Attend this must-see session to get an up-to-date refresh on how to create secure web applications and prevent the top ten issues from happening. Many code samples will demonstrate those risks, and countermeasures, to keep your applications secure.

speakers.name: Christian Wenz
speakers.bio: Christian Wenz is a consultant, software architect and entrepreneur specializing in web technologies and security. A prolific writer, he has authored or co-authored over 100 books for various publishers. Christian’s work spans both open-source and proprietary web technologies, a unique combination that has earned him recognition as a Microsoft MVP for Developer Technologies and the distinction of being the lead author of the Zend PHP certification. He is also credited in several open-source projects for his contributions. In addition to his writing and technical endeavors, Christian is a frequent speaker at developer conferences worldwide, where he shares his expertise in web technologies.

talks.title: Go with the Flow: Stop the Leaks Before Your Memory's a Waterfall!
talks.description:
You thought you didn't have tio think about memory management and memory leaks when you were done with C? Think again!

Join me starting the dive by looking at how golang allocates and deallocates memory, and the workings of the garbage collector. Learn how the stack and heap works. And why does my substring allocate so much memory?

We'll dip our toes into some pitfalls we all are guilty of, and some that are real edge cases. We're looking at quite a lot of code examples, and coding patterns. What can cause your application, website or k8s operator to consume increasingly amounts of memory? And how to avoid it without crashing out in a OOM (Out of memory) error?

And can I actually answer all of my own questions? Maybe more? Will you even know without joining in?

speakers.name: Manfred Bjørlin
speakers.bio:
Principal Cloud Native architect and developer with a passion for integration and automation. But wait, it's more! Passion does not only have to be in tech! There is also a burning passion for neurodiversity and diversity in tech, across ages, genders, identities, etc...

Loves integration, automation and making processes more streamlined. A back-end developer for over 20 years. Have worked with building integration platforms in the cloud for several bigger organizations.  Worked with .Net since early 2000, and Azure since launch.

Have also been a team lead, worked with process streamlining, enterprise architecture and everything between that and made my hands dirty as a developer and cloud native architect.

talks.title: Generative UIs and AI Assistants for Your Angular Applications
talks.description:
Copilot-style AI assistants are making their way into modern frontends: they guide users through processes, dramatically reduce task completion time, and answer questions through dynamically generated UIs.

In this session, you will learn how to integrate these capabilities into Angular applications. We show how the open-source solution Hashbrown connects LLMs with state management, the router, and forms to enable context-aware interactions. You will learn how client-side tool calling and generative UIs work—and what happens under the hood between your application and the LLM. This also highlights the strengths and weaknesses of the two libraries used.

By the end of the session, you will know how to extend your Angular applications with powerful AI assistants purposefully.

speakers.name: Manfred Steyer
speakers.bio: Trainer and Consultant with focus on Angular. Google Developer Expert (GDE) for Angular and Trusted Collaborator in the Angular team. Writes for O'Reilly, Hanser and the German Java Magazine. Regularly speaks at conferences.

talks.title: Parquet, Delta, Iceberg & Ducklake - An introduction for developers
talks.description:
CSVs are inefficient. Everyone knows that. And yet they are probably the most widely used file formats, also for data scientists. At the same time, data engineers talk about Parquet, Iceberg, and Ducklake—and roll their eyes when someone actually still uses CSV or JSON.

As a software engineer, there's often nothing left to do but close your eyes and go for it. Even if you don't really understand it. You read CSV, you write Delta or Iceberg. The main thing is that the data guys don't complain. But what are the differences? Why do we store data in files in the first place? What is all this metadata? And what do I really need and what not? And why can't just look onto storage but also have to take the compute into account. It's high time to dive in.

speakers.name: Matthias Niehoff
speakers.bio: Matthias Niehoff works as Head of Data and Data Architect for codecentric AG and supports customers in the design and implementation of data architectures. His focus is not so much on the ML model, but rather on the necessary infrastructure and organization to help data science projects succeed.

talks.title: Beyond authentication: an open-source trust model for the agentic web
talks.description:
Authenticating an agent tells you who it is, but not whether to let it transact, access data, or act on a user's behalf. As autonomous agents begin crossing organisational boundaries, the systems they reach face a binary choice: block all agent traffic or accept it without verification - neither of which scales as agent traffic grows.

TSAI (Trust Signals for Agentic Interactions) is an open source protocol that fills this gap. Built on W3C Verifiable Credentials and Decentralised Identifiers (DIDs), it carries trust signals beyond identity - reputation, economic stake, authorization, and endorsements - in cryptographically signed credentials that any system can verify offline. Independent Trust Authorities issue them and agents present them when accessing a service, while receiving systems make their own access decisions based on the signals. Credentials describe the agent, not the user, which preserves user privacy and keeps existing user authentication unchanged.

In this talk, we walk through the architecture - the four-tier trust model that scales from offline verification at low risk to real-time checks at high stakes, the credential format and lifecycle, and how TSAI composes with agent protocols like MCP and A2A. TSAI is developed by AWS and Trusted Shops, combining agent infrastructure expertise with decades of online trust certification.

speakers.name: Alexander Günsche
speakers.bio: Alex is a Senior Solutions Architect at AWS with 20 years of IT experience in expert and leadership roles. He is a strong advocate of agile and DevOps practices, and he enjoys seeing serverless, cloud-native and event-driven architectures deployed at scale. He has delivered large transformation projects and successfully developed own and customers’ businesses. As an international speaker, he has held advanced technology sessions at a wide range of events.

speakers.name: Sabrina Engling
speakers.bio:
Sabrina Engling leads the AI Solutions Team at Trusted Shops and drives AI adoption and innovation across the entire company. Her focus is on scalable AI solutions, AI operations, and agentic commerce. She combines technical expertise with strategic business acumen, bringing together both perspectives - from the architecture of scalable AI systems to business value.

Beyond her corporate role, Sabrina is a dedicated advocate for tech education and serves as Chairwoman of the NGO TechLabs, helping thousands of people build digital skills. As an AWS Commmunity Builder for AI Engineering, alumna of the AWS She Builds mentoring program, a certified AI Manager, and a recent AI hackathon winner, she is committed to empowering more women to take the leap into AI and cloud technologies.

talks.title: Future-Proofing Human Capital for the AI Economy
talks.description: Nobody knows what work, value or being "skilled" will even mean once AI reshapes the economy - yet we have to prepare for it anyway. This panel steps back from the day-to-day to ask the bigger question: how do people and societies stay relevant in a future none of us can predict? A forward-looking conversation about what endures when the rules are rewritten.

speakers.name: Grisha Pavlotskyi
speakers.bio: Grisha Pavlotskyi is the Chief Transformation Officer of Miro, the world’s leading visual workspace for innovation. Grisha spends most of his time with customers, helping them think through AI transformation topics - be it the technology side of it, ways of working, or how to re-engineer processes from an AI-first principles basis. Together with Miro's CIO, Grisha also drives Miro's own internal AI transformation. Prior to Miro, Grisha served as a Managing Partner at Deloitte for 19 years, focusing on helping organisations find ways to accelerate innovation.

speakers.name: Joël Mesot
speakers.bio: Joël Mesot has been President of ETH Zurich since 2019. At ETH he studied physics and obtained his doctorate with a thesis on high-temperature superconductors. He spent several years researching quantum materials in France, the USA and above all at the Swiss Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) where he was promoted to head the Laboratory for Neutron Scattering in 2004. In 2008 he became director of the PSI and was promoted full professor at ETH Zurich. Since taking office at ETH Zurich, Mesot has deepened dialogue with political actors both in Switzerland and internationally and driven forwards strategic fields such as AI, energy, space and cyber security.

speakers.name: Stephanie Cohen
speakers.bio: Stephanie Cohen joined Cloudflare in 2024 as the company’s first-ever Chief Strategy Officer. A seasoned operating executive, she brings more than two decades of experience at Goldman Sachs where she advised the leadership and boards of some of the world's most important companies and institutions. In addition to her time in Investment Banking, she was Goldman Sachs's Chief Strategy Officer, ran two multi-billion dollar global segments and served as a member of their Management Committee. In her role at Cloudflare, Stephanie leads the company's efforts in expanding the breadth and depth of its presence in boardrooms and the C-suite on its path to $5B in revenue and beyond.  She focuses on the most important initiatives driving Cloudflare's growth, including the future of the network, international expansion, AI and the developer platform. Stephanie has a Bachelors of Science in Finance from the University of Illinois.  She is a trustee for the Economic Club of New York and Park City Day School, a member of the Board of Quill.org and an Ambassador for US Ski & Snowboard.  She is also a member of the Board of Directors of Fiserv.

speakers.name: Stefan Lehmann
speakers.bio:
Stefan Lehmann was appointed Chief Executive Officer of Generali Deutschland as of September 2022 and is a member of the Group Management Committee of Assicurazioni Generali. He is responsible for the strategic direction of Generali Deutschland, which is one of the leading primary insurers in the German market, and is driving profitable growth, sustainable value creation, transformation across the organization and digitalization.

Stefan holds a degree in Economics from the University of Bochum and an Executive MBA in General & Strategic Management from the Maastricht School of Management. Prior to his studies, he completed a banking apprenticeship. Stefan started his professional career at WestLB Panmure Investment Banking in London and Düsseldorf.

Since 2004, he has held a series of senior management positions at Generali Deutschland, including Head of Participations Management, Head of Corporate Controlling & Development at Generali Deutschland Claims Management, Head of Customer Service at CosmosDirekt Versicherungen, and Head of Strategic Planning & Controlling of Generali Deutschland.

In 2017, Stefan was promoted to Chief Financial Officer of Generali Deutschland and in this role, he held different board roles in group companies. From January to August 2022, he was appointed Chief Business Officer Exclusive of Generali Deutschland with responsibility for the partnership with Deutsche Vermögensberatung AG. Since September 2022 he has been Chief Executive Officer of Generali Deutschland.

Since his appointment as CEO, Stefan has been shaping Generali Deutschland with a clear focus on profitable growth, sustainable value creation, cultural transformation, and digitalization. Under his leadership, the company has achieved significant profitable growth across all lines of business. At the same time, he drove a fundamental cultural transformation, repositioning Generali Deutschland from a more traditional insurance organization to a truly modern and attractive employer.

speakers.name: Fanny Jimenez
speakers.bio: Dr. Fanny Jimenez studied Psychology and Neuroscience in Berlin and the United States before earning her PhD at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin as part of the International Max Planck Research School. After several years in science journalism, she moved into media leadership and is now Vice President Performance & Collaboration at the PREMIUM Group (Politico Germany, WELT and Business Insider Germany), where she is responsible for newsroom effectiveness, organizational performance, and cross-brand collaboration and innovation.

talks.title: Edge Orchestration for the Physical World: Connecting Cameras, Sensors, and Devices with MQTT
talks.description:
You have cameras, sensors, or edge devices. You have custom scripts glueing them together. And somewhere in production, those scripts are quietly failing.

In 5 minutes, I'll show you what an edge orchestration layer looks like in practice — a single platform that connects mixed cameras and sensors, publishes events to MQTT, and gives you a browser dashboard with zero cloud dependency. Runs on Windows, Linux and Raspberry Pi. Free to start.

Four use cases, one architecture: Home Assistant makers unifying mixed-brand cameras without per-vendor apps; SMB operators getting Telegram alerts with video clips across multiple sites; AI teams running event-triggered multimodal capture for training data pipelines; and industrial sensing teams wrapping a processing module with dashboards, lifecycle management, and MQTT publishing — without touching the module itself.

speakers.name: Irina Terekhova
speakers.bio:
Irina Terekhova is Co-founder and Chief Product Officer at Banalytics, an open edge orchestration platform for cameras, sensors, and industrial devices.

At Banalytics she owns the product strategy, use-case definition, and roadmap across four customer segments: industrial sensing teams, AI data collection pipelines, SMB operations, and homelab builders. Her focus is on making edge infrastructure observable and deployable without requiring teams to build the operational layer from scratch.

Before Banalytics, Irina spent nearly two decades in product management and business analysis across AI, security, and financial services — including launching an AI line of business at an industrial hardware company and leading product teams at a global software consultancy.

talks.title: How One Developer Built the Back Office for 10 Million Companies
talks.description: EU just made time tracking legally mandatory for every employer in Europe. Nobody loves it, and most small businesses are stuck choosing between enterprise HR software they can't afford and free tools that fall apart the moment compliance is on the line. This talk is about building Pistacio, a full operations platform for companies under 200 people, as a solo engineer. I'll walk through the architecture decisions that let one person ship six production modules, how a shared foundation makes compliance structural rather than bolted on, and what it actually looks like to use AI as a force multiplier without letting the codebase turn into a mess.

speakers.name: Alija Nuredini
speakers.bio: Alija Nuredini is the Founder and CEO of Pistacio and DesignOps Lead at 8reasons Digital, a design agency. He built Pistacio to solve a problem he saw firsthand: service businesses juggling too many disconnected tools for time tracking, task management, expenses, and team coordination. Combining a founder's instinct with a builder's hands-on approach, he shipped a full operations platform serving real service teams. He has the scope decisions, dead ends, and lessons to prove it.

talks.title: Kill Your WordPress. Ship in Minutes. Win the SEO game.
talks.description:
We replaced a slow, dev-dependent WordPress/Elementor setup with a modern AI-native stack and didn't just ship faster. We won the SEO game too.

The stack: Lovable (AI page builder, locked to design system) → GitHub (version control + CI) → Cloudflare Pages + Workers (edge hosting) → Headless CMS (content teams self-serve, zero dev involvement).

In 5 minutes, you'll see how it works — two scenarios, one pipeline. We build a landing page with you and deploy it in minutes. A content editor publishes an article without touching a single line of code.

And the proof? We'll open Google Search Console live on stage.
Real outcomes: new pages ship in minutes, content teams are fully autonomous, hosting costs dropped, daily deployments became the norm, and organic traffic went through the roof.
Sounds too good to be true? It kind of is, and we are wondering why... Maybe you have the answer for us?

speakers.name: Malte Lensch
speakers.bio:
Malte Lensch started using Lovable and Claude in spring 2025, and it changed his life. What began as an experiment to rebuild his own consulting website turned into a production-grade workflow now running for multiple clients.

Mainly helping companies now kill their WordPress and Webflow setups and replace them with modern AI-native stacks that actually ship.

He's Managing Director at Till Freitag Consulting, a Berlin-based consultancy specialising in AI-native workflows and automation. In his spare time, he is spending more and more time in the garden.

talks.title: AIQSpecFlow: Improves and automates your agile process of specification and creation of testcases.
talks.description: Good software starts with clear requirements. Discover how AIQSpecFlow helps you automatically create structured epics and user stories, right where others are still sorting and formulating theirs. AIQSpecFlow identifies gaps in test case coverage, assists with the creation of test cases in natural language, and enables the generation of executable test cases for various test frameworks. Higher quality and significantly less manual effort.

speakers.name: Rene Schenk
speakers.bio: René is a software architect and lead developer at iQMatix. For more than 20 years, René has been helping clients in the insurance, healthcare and retail sectors with architectural decisions, design and implementation.

talks.title: The integrated AI experience: A New Paradigm in an Agentic World
talks.description: When agents start acting on people's behalf, the customer is no longer the only one you are designing systems for. This panel asks what changes when products are built for agents as much as for humans, and what that means for brands and experience. A look at how the basics of commerce and product shift in an agentic world.

speakers.name: Loredana Crisan
speakers.bio: Loredana Crisan is the Chief Design Officer at Figma, where she leads design, UX writing, brand studio and research. Prior to joining Figma, she spent nine years at Meta, where she held product and design leadership roles across Messenger, Instagram and GenAI initiatives. Before Loredana’s career in product and design, she was a musician and sound engineer.

speakers.name: Markus Rautert
speakers.bio: Markus Rautert is Chief Technology Officer at adidas, where he leads global technology strategy across enterprise architecture, platform engineering, IT infrastructure, cybersecurity, and Data & AI. With nearly two decades at adidas, Markus has helped build the company’s digital backbone—scaling platforms, securing operations, and enabling data-driven decisions across brand, supply chain, and finance. His current focus is on strengthening cybersecurity and unlocking business value through advanced analytics. Markus speaks regularly at internal and industry events, connecting with developers and senior leaders alike. Offstage, he’s a lifelong gamer and passionate tech enthusiast.

speakers.name: Stefan Ostwald
speakers.bio: Stefan Ostwald is Chief AI Officer and Co-Founder of Parloa, a leading AI company redefining customer service through AI agents. Stefan's passion for conversational AI dates back to 2016, when he co-founded Future of Voice — one of Europe's first voice AI agencies. In 2018, he went on to found Parloa, where he now leads the agentic AI research team, bridging state-of-the-art research with enterprise-grade solutions. His mission: making AI so reliable and intuitive that every conversation deepens the customer relationship.

speakers.name: Anna Heim
speakers.bio: Anna Heim is a freelance reporter at TechCrunch and event moderator focusing on tech and startups, with a keen eye for innovation outside of Silicon Valley. Her byline has appeared in publications including CNet, Fortune, Resilience Media and The Next Web. A former startup founder and Sciences Po Paris alum, she is fluent in multiple languages, including French, English, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese.

talks.title: From Global Capability Centers to AI-Powered Command Centers
talks.description:
Building Intelligent Enterprise Operations with AI, Automation and Decision
Intelligence
Global Capability Centers are evolving into AI-powered innovation hubs, driving the next generation of enterprise operations. This session explores how enterprise architecture, AI, automation, and decision intelligence can be combined to build intelligent command centers that enable faster, more informed decision-making. Designed for developers, architects, and technology leaders, it highlights the key architectural, implementation, and governance considerations for deploying scalable, enterprise-ready AI solutions.

speakers.name: Sandeep Kusuma
speakers.bio: Sandeep Kusuma is an Enterprise AI and Technology Leader at Bosch Global Software Technologies, based in Germany, with more than two decades of experience helping enterprises turn digital transformation into measurable business value. His background spans enterprise technology, Industry 4.0, IoT, AI, and large-scale delivery, with experience shaped by work across European and Indian business ecosystems and global capability center aligned delivery models.
