Before joining Dynatrace, Gala founded a venture-backed startup and has spent her career building products, leading global teams, and turning complex technical challenges into intuitive experiences .She is passionate about the intersection of AI, observability, and product design, creating products that engineers genuinely love to use.

talks.title: Can SVG be fast? Rendering a scatter chart with over 10k points
talks.description:
In this talk, we’ll explore the performance limits of SVG when rendering scatter charts with thousands of data points, based on our experience at MUI X Charts.

You’ll learn how to identify bottlenecks, performance measuring tricks, and the techniques we use to optimize rendering.

speakers.name: Bernardo Belchior
speakers.bio: Bernardo is a software engineer working on the MUI X Charts team to build the next-generation of React charts. He likes performance work and data visualization in general (charts, maps, etc.) and is very excited to have the opportunity to improve the ecosystem of charting in the web.

talks.title: Multiple Apps, Millions of Users: Scaling React Native in Production
talks.description:
What happens when a React Native app becomes multiple apps serving millions of users? You learn a lot, sometimes the hard way.

It started with a single mobile app. Today, multiple high-traffic products serve millions of users across Europe, all built with React Native. This talk shares the real lessons from that evolution: the architectural decisions that paid off, the performance challenges along the way, and the upgrade nightmares that had to be survived.

Expect to hear what worked, what didn't, and what should have been done differently.

speakers.name: Milica Aleksic
speakers.bio:
I’m a senior software engineer with expertise in mobile development, particularly React Native. I focus on building performant, scalable applications and a great user experience.

Beyond code, I’m passionate about community and mentorship. As co-founder of Women in Tech Niš, I organize events, mentor aspiring professionals, and advocate for diversity in tech. I’ve also spoken at international conferences and hosted large-scale events as an MC, combining technical knowledge with clear and engaging communication.

I am driven, detail-oriented, and always learning. I bring a mix of technical depth, people-centered leadership, and a genuine love for building things that matter.

talks.title: Outclassing Frontier LLMs at Extracting Information
talks.description:
Accurately extracting information from documents has been a decades-old dream. Many important workflows, from automated back-office processing to enterprise RAG, depend on it. General-purpose LLMs promise to fulfill this dream, but they have drawbacks: they make mistakes, are expensive, and are difficult to use privately.

The solution: specialized LLMs, built specifically for document extraction.

In this talk, I will present NuExtract3, the leading document-extraction LLM specialized in both structured extraction (turning documents into JSON following a schema) and OCR (turning documents into clean Markdown). I will demonstrate its capabilities, discuss what makes it different from general-purpose LLMs, and show how developers can use it either through its open-source version or through the NuExtract Platform.

speakers.name: Etienne Bernard
speakers.bio: Etienne is an AI/ML expert, co-founder & CEO of NuMind — a startup developing LLMs specialized in information extraction. Etienne holds a physics PhD (ENS+MIT), led the ML group of Wolfram Research, and wrote Introduction to Machine Learning.

talks.title: The End of Commit-Fail-Commit: Rethinking CI with AI Agents and GitHub Actions
talks.description: Your pipelines automate the predictable. But what about triaging issues, reviewing PRs, responding to incidents, and coordinating across tools? See what's new in GitHub Actions and how it's becoming the execution layer for AI agents across your dev lifecycle. We'll cover agent-triggered workflows, MCP server integration, and automated handoffs that keep humans in the loop — plus how to finally break the 'commit - see CI fail - commit again' loop.

speakers.name: Ben De St Paer-Gotch
speakers.bio: Ben De St Paer-Gotch is the Director of Product at GitHub, where he oversees the strategic vision and development for core developer tools including GitHub Actions, Packages, Codespaces, Microsoft Dev Tunnels, and npm. Driven by a mission to improve developers' lives, Ben leads his teams in building seamless solutions that automate day-to-day workflows. speakers.name: Julia Kordick

talks.title: The New AI Security Stack: Observe, Detect, Protect

speakers.name: Jyoti Bansal
speakers.bio: Jyoti Bansal is a multi-unicorn founder and serial technology entrepreneur. He has been recognized as EY Entrepreneur of the Year, Forbes' Best Cloud Computing CEO, SiliconANGLE's Most Innovative Tech Startup Leader, and ranked No. 24 on Fortune's Most Innovative Companies list. speakers.name: Christian Trummer
speakers.bio: Christian Trummer is the founder and Chief Scientist of Bitpanda. Previously serving as CTO for nearly a decade, he scaled the engineering team to over 400 people, building the company's core trading platform and in-house banking system. He now leads a specialized team focused on embedding AI across the organization to enhance products and efficiency. Christian combines deep technical expertise with a vision for AI-driven transformation in fintech.

speakers.name: Tomislav Tipurić
speakers.bio: Tomislav Tipurić is a business and technology professional who connects technical expertise with business strategy to clarify new technologies and drive corporate innovation. As a Chief Technology Officer and Lead Hackathon Coach, he focuses on artificial intelligence, multi-cloud platforms, and modern software development practices. speakers.name: Milin Desai
speakers.bio: Milin Desai currently serves as the CEO of Sentry. Used by more than 4 million developers and 150,000 organizations worldwide, Sentry helps every developer detect, understand, and fix broken code, fast. Milin joined Sentry from VMware where he helped build out multiple lines of business from networking (0->1b+) to multi cloud (0->100M+ SAAS). talks.title: API, MCP or MCP App? Choosing the right surface for AI agents
talks.description:
AI-referred shoppers convert 54% higher and generate 53% more revenue per visit than non-AI traffic (Adobe, May 2026). AI sessions to retailers grew 138% year-over-year. As the customer journey collapses into a single conversation, "build an API" stops being the obvious answer when the consumer isn't a developer but an agent.

This talk distills what we learned shipping to ChatGPT, Claude, and our own internal agents – and the framework we use to decide what to build for whom.

API, MCP, and MCP App are three different products serving three different consumers: a developer building their own integration, an agent runtime where the host owns the UI, and an app surface where the UI returns but is shared with the model. Treating MCP as a drop-in replacement for an API is how teams end up with a tool surface their agents can't actually use.

From there, four engineering lessons stand out that don't appear in the MCP spec:

– Tool descriptions are prompts, not docs. A one-line change can flip whether the model calls your tool, or calls it with hallucinated arguments.

– Flow is a design surface. You're not designing tools in isolation – you're designing the path the model walks through them.

– Treat your tool surface like a prompt: version it, snapshot it, eval it. Unit tests don't catch the failures that matter.

– In an MCP app, the UI is part of the prompt. Widget state pushes back to the model as context; tools split between model-visible and widget-only – a new design discipline with little prior art.

Attendees leave with a decision framework for the three-way call, and a practical checklist for shipping a tool surface that agents can actually use.

speakers.name: Rishabh Budhiraja
speakers.bio:
Rishabh Budhiraja is Staff Engineer at idealo, specializing in cloud-native web applications, frontend modernization, performance engineering, and agentic system development. He works on high-traffic customer-facing systems across checkout and offer page experiences, building scalable features and improving user experience through experimentation and modern architecture.

His work includes migrating legacy frontend systems to modern micro frontend architectures, optimizing Core Web Vitals, contributing to idealo’s company-wide frontend framework, and exploring MCP-based integrations for AI-enabled engineering workflows. With experience across React, Astro, AWS, Kubernetes, server-side rendering, and AI-assisted development, Rishabh focuses on building robust, scalable systems that help teams deliver faster and create better digital experiences.

speakers.name: Rishi Deorukhkar
speakers.bio:
Rishi Deorukhkar is AI Engineer at idealo specializing in AI-native systems, backend architecture, and cloud platform development. He builds agentic RAG pipelines, MCP applications, AI agents, and evaluation frameworks for automated compliance, audit workflows, document intelligence, and developer productivity.

His work spans scalable APIs, vector databases, specification-driven coding agents, enterprise SaaS platforms, and eval-driven AI systems deployed across AWS and Azure. With experience in TypeScript, Python, LangChain, OpenAI, Claude, CDK, Pulumi, Kubernetes, and microservices architecture, Rishi focuses on turning complex business workflows into reliable, automated, AI-powered systems.

talks.title: Beyond Webhooks: The Future of Scalable API Event Delivery
talks.description:
Since Jeff Lindsay introduced webhooks in 2007, they’ve become the default mechanism for delivering API platform events to consuming applications. But as adoption has surged and event-driven systems have evolved, the cracks in the webhook model have started to show—scalability challenges, reliability concerns, and operational overhead are just the tip of the iceberg.
In this talk, I’ll challenge the status quo and explore why webhooks may no longer be the best fit for modern API platform event delivery. More importantly, I’ll introduce Event Destinations—a Stripe-inspired next-generation approach designed to handle event distribution at scale, offering greater flexibility, resilience, and control. If you’re building APIs or event-driven platforms, this session will equip you with the insights to rethink your event delivery strategy.

speakers.name: Phil Leggetter
speakers.bio:
Phil Leggetter is an experienced Developer Experience, Developer Relations, and DevTools PLG leader with a background guiding startups through growth, acquisition, and scale within a publicly traded enterprise.

He has spent his career building software experiences that maximize developer productivity at companies such as Pusher (acquired by MessageBird), Nexmo (acquired by Vonage), and, most recently, Hookdeck, where he helps build platforms and tools that empower developers to create interoperable and dependable event-driven systems.

talks.title: The Hidden Cost of AI Coding: Technical Debt You Can’t See
talks.description: AI coding tools boost your productivity today, but at what price? This session uncovers the invisible technical debt accumulating in codebases built with AI assistants. Explore how generated code creates maintenance nightmares, why test coverage doesn’t tell the whole story, and what happens when your team can’t explain how their own code works. Learn to spot warning signs early, implement measures that preserve code quality, and build systems you can actually debug.

speakers.name: Maish Saidel-Keesing
speakers.bio:
Maish Saidel-Keesing is a Senior Developer Advocate at AWS.

He's been working in tech for over 20 years, and if there's one thing that's been consistent throughout his career, it's this: if something can be automated, it should be. He's an automation junkie. Always has been.

He helps developers build in the cloud. Not by talking at them, but by building with them. He live-codes at meetups. He writes. He speaks. He creates. He's got a blog with over 700 posts because he genuinely believes that when you share what you've learned, everybody wins.

What gets him excited right now is the intersection of GenAI and developer workflows. Not the hype. The practical stuff. How do you actually use these tools to ship faster, automate your infrastructure, and focus on the code that matters? That's what he helps people figure out.

He works with everyone from students writing their first lines of code to senior engineers architecting complex distributed systems. Dev communities. Academic institutions. Because making cutting-edge tools accessible to everyone is the whole point.

His mission is simple. Equip developers with the knowledge, tools, and confidence to build anything they can imagine in the cloud.

talks.title: Testing AI Agents: Automated Evaluation for Chatbots & RAG Systems
talks.description:
AI Agents, chatbots, and RAG systems are easy to prototype — but difficult to test reliably. Small changes to prompts, models, retrieval sources, or system instructions can silently change behavior, and classic assertions (string matching, snapshots) often fail to capture what actually matters: correctness, relevance, grounded answers, and consistent multi-turn dialogue.

In this talk, we’ll start with the common testing problems in real projects: “it worked yesterday”, hidden regressions, evaluation noise, and the challenge of aligning developers and stakeholders on what “good” means.

Then we’ll explore practical testing possibilities with evaluation frameworks like DeepEval: how to validate responses beyond keyword matching, how to structure test cases for both chatbots and retrieval-based assistants, how to define pragmatic quality gates, and how to run these checks continuously in suggests, then?

As a side topic, we’ll show how BDD/Gherkin can wrap these evaluations into human-readable scenarios (Given–When–Then), making expectations reviewable by non-developers while keeping the actual validation powered by automated evaluation metrics.

You’ll leave with a reusable blueprint for introducing automated AI evaluation into your development workflow — from local runs to CI pipelines with actionable reports.

speakers.name: Sebastian Messingfeld
speakers.bio: Sebastian is a Staff Engineer at Eurowings Digital GmbH, building end-to-end solutions across the Eurowings website and mobile app. His current focus is the information experience on eurowings.com — including AI-powered chatbots, on-site search, and smarter contact flows — where he helps teams turn AI features into reliable, production-ready capabilities.

speakers.bio: Yuval Dvir

speakers.name: Marcus Hennig
speakers.bio:
Dr. Marcus Hennig serves as Chief Business Officer at planqc, where he is responsible for the strategic development and implementation of quantum solutions. In this role, he operates at the intersection of high-performance computing, technology, and business innovation.

A physicist with a background in mathematical finance, he contributed to international research projects in France, China, and Australia before spending more than a decade in consulting, supporting companies in the development and implementation of new business models.

With his experience in building innovation units and his deep expertise in quantum computing and emerging technologies, Hennig combines scientific excellence with strong business execution capabilities. His mission is to help companies strategically leverage quantum computing to drive growth, efficiency, and sustainable competitive advantage.

talks.title: Garbage In, Garbage Out: Engineering Reliable AI Document Extraction Pipelines
talks.description:
Your OCR problem isn't really an OCR problem. It’s everything that happens before and after it.

Most AI pipelines don’t fail because the model is bad. They fail because we send it garbage. We throw blurry mobile scans, crooked receipts, and massive blocks of unstructured text at an LLM and wonder why it’s expensive, inconsistent, and hallucinatory.



In this talk, you’ll see how to design an end-to-end document extraction pipeline that:

Validates and improves image quality at capture time

Extracts structured, high-context data instead of dumping raw text

Sends lean, intentional payloads to LLMs so they’re cheaper and more predictable

speakers.name: Nazeer Saeed
speakers.bio:
With over a decade of experience in solution engineering, consulting, and digital transformation, I help organizations design scalable technology solutions that solve complex business challenges.

At Apryse, I work with enterprises and development teams on document processing, OCR, SDK integrations, workflow automation, and AI-driven extraction pipelines. My focus is on building reliable, secure, and efficient systems that turn unstructured documents into actionable data.

My background spans R&D in AI, knowledge management, and Industry 4.0 across Europe. As a speaker, I share practical engineering patterns that help developers build smarter, more predictable document AI solutions.

talks.title: Swapping a Data Warehouse at Runtime: Zero-Downtime Migration Without Changing a Single Client
talks.description:
Trade Republic serves 10 million with €150 billion under management. Our data warehouse handles 4 million queries daily across analytics, product features, and the ML fraud detection that protects our customers. It replicates 220 databases into a 620 TB lakehouse. It cannot go down.

Moving to an open lakehouse architecture — Apache Iceberg & bring-your-own-compute  — "schedule a maintenance window" was not an option. Neither was asking hundreds of consumers — BI tools, pipelines, ML models, product services — to rewrite their connections.

The destination: decoupled storage-compute where teams choose the engine that fits their workload. Spark, Athena, DuckDB — all reading from the Iceberg. But the migration path matters as much as the destination.

Our approach: "Engy" build a protocol-compatible proxy that presents the exact wire interface of our existing warehouse. Every client connects the same way it always has. Behind that stable interface, we're free to change everything: swap compute engines, cache, add features — all invisible to consumers.

The key enabler is in-flight SQL transpilation. The proxy rewrites SQL, translates table references between catalogs, and normalises result, all in the request path. This gives us a multi-engine architecture with perfect interop.

Teams onboard without changing a driver, a connection string, or a line of code. We ship new engines and features behind the interface while production traffic is flowing — building the plane as we fly it. The interface becomes a contract that decouples the pace of infrastructure evolution from the pace of consumer adoption.

In this talk I'll walk through how we designed the Engy proxy interface for long-term stability that lets us migrate a 620 TB system query-by-query without downtime.

True to Trade Republic's engineering philosophy, the entire stack is built on open-source foundations — no vendor tooling, no proprietary middleware.

speakers.name: Max Fischer
speakers.bio:
Director Engineering Trade Republic, responsible for the Engineering, Data and Cyber Security organisation.
Earlier CTO Bluestep Bank, VP Klarna, Executive VP Nordea, Chief Business Architect SEB, Chief Architect TeliaSonera

speakers.name: Michael O'Toole
speakers.bio: Michael O'Toole is a Staff Engineer at Trade Republic. Over the past decade he's been building, breaking, and migrating data platforms across Europe and across the pong. When he's not obsessing over query performance, he plays in TwoFoxOut. He brings the same energy to both — loud, fast, and no unnecessary downtime.

talks.title: 11 Principles for Evaluating AI Dev Tools
talks.description:
Benchmarks measure narrow capabilities. Demos show best-case scenarios. Neither tells you whether AI-generated code will survive production or whether that shiny new tool deserves a place in your stack.

This talk presents a unified framework of 11 principles for evaluating AI-generated code and the tools that manage it. Because code quality and tool quality are inseparable: bad tools generate bad code, and bad code evaluation processes never catch it.

We'll reframe AI use with responsibility boundaries where the core questions shift from "is it fast?" to "can this be understood under pressure, safely changed, and defended to a stakeholder?"

Through real-world patterns from teams adopting AI across their SDLC, we'll apply these principles to distinguish tools that surface risk from tools that hide it.

Attendees will leave with a practical rubric to decide which AI tools to trust, which to constrain, and how to keep human judgment at the center of fast-moving, AI-augmented engineering.

speakers.name: Nnenna Ndukwe
speakers.bio: Nnenna Ndukwe is a Principal Developer Advocate and Software Engineer, passionate about AI. With 8+ experience spanning across media tech, cybersecurity, and AI, she's an active global AI community architect championing engineers to build in emerging tech. She studied Computer Science at Boston University and is a proud member of Women Defining AI and Reg.exe. Nnenna believes that AI should augment: enabling creativity, accelerating learning, and preserving the intuition and humanity of its users.

talks.title: Beyond Chat: AI Workflows That Actually Investigate Alerts (So You Don't Have To Know Everything)
talks.description:
"You build it, you run it" sounds great until you're on-call for a Kafka consumer lag spike at 3 AM—and you spent the last six months building the React frontend, not the event pipeline. Modern teams own their services end-to-end, but no one can be an expert in everything. And the AI chatbots we've been promised? They just add another window to alt-tab through while the pager screams.

This talk argues that chat-based AI is fundamentally wrong for incident investigation. I'll break down why the chat paradigm fails: it expects you to provide context you don't have at 3 AM, assumes you know where to look, burns time with back-and-forth, and interrogates instead of investigates.

Then I'll show what actually works: AI workflows that investigate like a teammate who knows the system—automatically discovering affected resources, correlating metrics with deployments, querying the right logs without being asked, and delivering hypotheses with evidence.

We'll cover real engineering challenges: orchestrating tools across Kubernetes, logs, and metrics; solving the "where do I even start?" problem; building outputs that explain unfamiliar systems; and what breaks when you let AI loose on production.

Live Demo: A simulated 3 AM alert comparing the chatbot experience ("Can you tell me more about your cluster configuration?") versus a workflow that delivers: "Your deployment rolled out 47 minutes ago with a memory limit reduction. Three pods are OOMKilling. Here's the diff and the kubectl command to rollback."

speakers.name: Aram Hakobyan
speakers.bio: Platform Engineering Lead and Infrastructure Expert with over 25 years of experience designing and operating highly scalable, distributed systems. Currently serving as Head of Platform Engineering at zooplus SE, where I lead container orchestration and observability teams, running 40 k8s clusters and 3000 microservices, supporting one of Europe's largest online pet retailers.

speakers.name: Nune Isabekyan
speakers.bio:
Nune Isabekyan is a Berlin-based founder and cloud architecture expert with over 15 years of experience building scalable, intelligent systems. With a mathematics background and deep expertise in AWS, AI, and DevOps, she specializes in practical AI implementation and cloud-native architectures.
As founder and CTO of OpsWorker, Nune is building AI-powered alert investigation automation. When an alert fires, OpsWorker automatically investigates, pulls logs, checks dashboards, correlates events, and gives on-call engineers a summary of what's wrong and suggested next steps. Previously, as CIO of powerdata GmbH, she led teams building SaaS products and AI-powered customer service automation for the utilities sector. Her earlier career includes engineering roles at Teradata, Amadeus, and high-scale startups handling millions of daily users.

talks.title: From Vague Ideas to Precise Specifications – AI as Process Catalyst
talks.description: We've all been there: clients know what they want but struggle to articulate it. Teams interpret requirements differently. Half the specs are missing. This talk explores how language models help transform this chaos into structured user stories. Through live demos, I'll share practical prompting strategies that actually work. Spoiler alert: AI isn't a miracle cure, it's an intelligent sparring partner. Developers remain essential – because only they truly understand the context. Let's dive into how AI amplifies your requirements process without replacing your expertise.

speakers.name: Patrick Schnell
speakers.bio: Patrick Schnell is a distinguished computer scientist and acclaimed author specializing in the integration of AI into software development and business-processes. With a solid foundation in computer science and software-projects, Patrick has dedicated his career to exploring the transformative potential of AI and Large Language Models (LLMs) within the software industry. His team established Vectense (www.vectense.com) as an AI-automation-platform for small and mid-sized businesses.

talks.title: Data: The Deciding Factor in AI Success
talks.description: Most AI projects do not fail on the model - they fail on the data underneath it. This panel makes the case that data is what really decides whether AI succeeds, and digs into what teams consistently get wrong. Leaders who work at the foundation share where it actually breaks.

speakers.name: Damandeep Kochhar
speakers.bio: Damandeep Kochhar is EVP, Chief Platform & Technology Officer at HERE Technologies. In his role, he leads the company’s core engineering activities, including the development and operation of our highly automated mapping system for creating, updating and publishing map content.

speakers.name: Jörg Tewes
speakers.bio: Joerg Tewes joined Exasol as CEO at the beginning of 2023. He spent the first 12 years of his career at data management software company Poet Holdings supporting the company through its early growth stages to its IPO at the German stock exchange. He relocated to the San Francisco Bay Area in 2007 and continued to pursue his career in general management roles at Avid Technology Inc. and Logitech International. In 2014, he joined video and augmented reality start-up Avegant as CEO, where he raised $50M in venture capital funding and strategically expanded the company’s product offerings. From 2018 – 2022, Joerg Tewes held senior leadership roles at Amazon, driving the development and commercialization of its tablet, e-reader and video communication technologies. Joerg Tewes is an active angel investor and mentor to technology start-ups. He holds a degree in computer science from the Technical University in Berlin, Germany.

speakers.name: Siddhika Nevrekar
speakers.bio:
Siddhika Nevrekar is senior director of product management at Qualcomm Technologies, where she is responsible for product and AI software development, including Qualcomm AI Hub.

Siddhika Nevrekar is a visionary product leader with expertise in AI and machine learning. Siddhika co-founded Tetra AI, which was later acquired by Qualcomm.

Prior to Tetra AI, she worked to steer CoreML at Apple and spearheaded the development of a Classification Machine Learning Platform at Microsoft. Her work has revolutionized key technologies across major platforms such as Bing, Siri, and now the Qualcomm AI Hub.

Siddhika received an MBA in International Business from the Institute of Technology and Management, India and a Bachelor of Computer Engineering from Vivekanand Education Society’s Institute of Technology.

speakers.name: Ed Huang
speakers.bio: Co-founder & CTO at PingCAP (the company behind TiDB), an entrepreneur with a hacker's mind & heart. Full-stack engineer, for real. Pioneer in building cloud-native systems. Building distributed systems and databases with ♥️. Building a company like a distributed system.

speakers.name: Laura Moritz
speakers.bio:
Laura Moritz is a Tech Manager for Data & AI at Globant, where she leads AI and data programs for enterprise clients across industries including automotive, healthcare, finance, and education. With 10 years of consulting experience, she works at the intersection of AI strategy, data products, and implementation — from LLM-powered solutions and predictive models to data platforms and analytics.
Beyond her corporate work, Laura is engaged with Women in Tech, supporting initiatives that bring more women in technology onto stages and into leadership.

talks.title: The AI Velocity Trap: Shipping Faster Without Breaking More
talks.description:
LLMs and coding agents have made it dramatically easier to produce code. But if every velocity gain also increases regressions, incidents, and error rates, we have not improved software delivery; we have only moved the bottleneck downstream.

I'll explore:

Why AI-assisted velocity is a liability without stronger feedback loops.
How agents can harden the lifecycle before, during, and after code is written.
How an agent team can verify plans, inspect changes, challenge assumptions, and catch issues before human review.
How deployment awareness and production monitoring change the role of coding agents.
How teams can ship faster without turning every release into a reliability gamble.
The new SDLC loop: moving from requirements → build → verify → observe → repeat.

speakers.name: Ohans Emmanuel
speakers.bio: Staff software engineer and technical author with 5+ published books. Since 2017, he’s written extensively about software and product development, with his work reaching 5M+ readers. He specialises in turning complex problems into simple, reliable systems and building delightful user interfaces that hold up in the real world.

talks.title: Measuring the Wrong Things Faster Than Ever
talks.description:
Tokenmaxxing. Bloated PRs. Endless tiny commits.
We already know how easily developer productivity metrics can be gamed. So why are token spend and AI-generated lines of code becoming the default way to measure the impact of agentic coding tools?
As AI become part of everyday work for most developers, engineering leaders are under pressure to prove impact. Many organizations are falling back on familiar, easy-to-measure metrics, even when those metrics miss the real value AI creates.
At the same time, AI is shifting from automation to augmentation: not just helping developers code faster, but changing how teams think, collaborate, and make decisions. That means the old models for measuring productivity and ROI may no longer apply.
Join Laura Tacho for a research-backed look at how AI is reshaping developer productivity.

speakers.name: Laura Tacho
speakers.bio: Laura Tacho is a subject matter expert in measuring the efficiency of engineering organizations. Currently, she is a Senior Principal Technologist at AWS focusing on developer experience and AI-native development. Laura was previously the CTO of DX, where she led the company’s executive advisory and research programs. She is the co-author of the Core 4 Framework of Developer Productivity, used by companies like LEGO, Netflix, Airbnb, Pinterest, and Snowflake to measure and improve developer experience. In 2025, she was awarded Austrian Innovator of the Year. Laura’s been working on developer tools for 15 years, including building out some of the first developer tools for the Docker ecosystem.

talks.title: MFA? Game over! Watch your protection collapse – live
talks.description:
In a digital world where passwords and multi-factor authentication are considered impenetrable defenses, reality looks quite different. Every month, millions of attacks bypass these very security mechanisms. Yet, many still believe that MFA guarantees complete security.
In this talk, I will demonstrate live how effortlessly passwords can be stolen and MFA mechanisms bypassed. And the best part? It’s free, can be set up and executed in just a few minutes, and becomes even easier with the use of AI. I will show that the biggest weakness is often not the technology itself, but the trust we place in it.
However, there are solutions. When technological advancements and human vigilance work together effectively, the attack surface for hackers shrinks significantly.

speakers.name: Christoph Menzel
speakers.bio:
Christoph Menzel is Head of Security Excellence at inovex. With more than 15 years of experience in software development, he combines practical developer expertise with security know-how from technical, strategic, and business perspectives.
His clear goal is to help organizations understand security not as a burden, but as an integral part of software development.
As a speaker, trainer, coach, and author, Christoph regularly shares his practical, field-tested knowledge. His hands-on mentality and focus on sustainable solutions make him a valuable partner for companies looking to take their software security to the next level.

talks.title: Your Kubernetes Node Is Not a Server: Rethinking the OS Layer
talks.description:
Kubernetes already treats nodes as disposable, but most platform stacks still run them as long-lived servers. This mismatch creates unnecessary complexity in upgrades, security, and operations, especially for edge, bare-metal, and high-churn environments.

In this talk, I’ll present an alternative model: treating Kubernetes worker nodes as firmware, not operating systems. Using k0s, Linux Unified Kernel Images (UKI), and an initramfs-only OS, we build immutable workers that boot entirely from RAM, fetch configuration from metadata (cloud-init style), and optionally persist state using a single mounted /var directory.

speakers.name: Natanael Copa
speakers.bio: Natanael Copa is the creator of Alpine Linux and a maintainer of the k0s Kubernetes distribution. He has over 20 years of experience in Linux and open-source infrastructure, with a focus on minimal, secure systems.

talks.title: Football for Good: Hackathon Finals - Live Pitches & Awards
talks.description: The top hackathon teams take the stage to pitch their Football for Good AI agent prototypes to a panel of technical influencer judges. Each finalist delivers a 5-minute live pitch covering their problem statement, working demo, agentic architecture, and real-world social impact. Judges deliberate and winners are announced live on stage. Come watch the best agent-powered solutions built over 3 days compete for the prize pool.

speakers.name: Salih Guler
speakers.bio: Salih is a Senior Developer Advocate at AWS and Google Developer Expert with over 10 years of experience spanning fullstack, mobile, and cloud development. He specializes in bridging complex engineering challenges with developer communities through hands-on code, content, and technical strategy.

talks.title: Building Organizations That Can Actually Adapt
talks.description:
In a world defined by constant disruption, from AI-driven transformation and shifting workforce expectations to economic uncertainty and rapid technological change, organizational adaptability has become a critical competitive advantage. Yet many companies still struggle to move beyond agility as a buzzword and build the structures, cultures, and leadership practices that enable real, sustained adaptation.

Join Claudia Tatanelli as she moderates an engaging discussion with Kerstin Wagner, Anastasia Removic, and Nazim Ünlü, three leaders at the forefront of organizational transformation. Together, they will explore what it takes to create organizations that can continuously evolve, learn, and thrive in times of change.

The panel will examine how leaders can foster resilience, empower teams to make decisions, balance stability with innovation, and build cultures that embrace experimentation without losing focus. Attendees will gain practical insights into the strategies, mindsets, and operating models that help organizations respond effectively to today's challenges while preparing for tomorrow's opportunities.

speakers.name: Anastasija Removic
speakers.bio: Anastasija Removic

speakers.name: Claudia Tattanelli
speakers.bio: Claudia Tattanelli is the Founder and CEO of C-YourCulture and the Chairwoman of the global think tank Future Talent Council. Formerly, Claudia was the Chairwoman of the Universum Strategic Board, and for over 25 years she has led many culture and employer branding strategy projects, supporting the leadership teams of many of the world's leading companies, including Accenture, Alexander McQueen, Apple, AB InBev, Audi, Barclays, Barilla, Campari, Citibank, Coca-Cola, Coty, Exxon, EY, Facebook, FedEx, H&M, Goldman Sachs, Google, IBM, JPMorgan, Luxottica, Lamborghini, L’Oréal, Mondelēz, Lenovo, P&G, SAP, Siemens, the United Nations, Unilever, YSL, and Zalando. Claudia is a regular keynote speaker at conferences and events worldwide and has been quoted in many leading newspapers, journals, and podcasts, including Businessweek, CNN, The New York Times, Financial Times, Forbes, Fortune, The Washington Post, Il Sole 24 Ore, Corriere della Sera, and The Economist. Claudia has also been a guest on Bloomberg, Fox, and CNBC’s Morning Call, as well as many other media outlets.

speakers.name: Kerstin Wagner
speakers.bio:
At Deutsche Bahn AG, Kerstin Wagner serves as Executive Vice President of Talent Acquisition, reporting directly to the Chief Human Resources Officer. In this role, she consolidates recruiting, employer branding, global governance, and temporary employment under one roof. Her primary objective is to position DB as a top employer and attract talent to the DB Group.

Working with her team, she oversees the recruitment of a workforce equivalent to the size of a small town every year, while ensuring the talent acquisition process remains innovative and modern. Kerstin Wagner is a member of several supervisory boards and chairs the Advisory Board of the Deutsche Bahn Foundation. Additionally, she is a dedicated advocate for New Work, technology, and diversity.

In 2021, she was named one of the "100 Women of the Year" by Focus magazine, and in 2024, Personalmagazin recognized her as one of the 50 most influential HR thought leaders.

speakers.name: Nazim Ünlü
speakers.bio: Nazim Ünlü

talks.title: Context Graphs for Explainable, Decision-Aware AI Agents
talks.description:
AI agents can follow prompts and use tools, but often lack the institutional context needed to explain why a decision is made. That reasoning: policies, precedents, and past outcomes are usually scattered across systems and human memory.
Context graphs capture this missing layer by modeling decision traces over time, including causality and context. By giving agents access to just enough historical and organizational knowledge, context graphs enable more explainable, consistent, and auditable decisions.

speakers.name: Zaid Zaim
speakers.bio: As a Developer Advocate at Neo4j, I help developers harness the power of graph technology and AI. A Microsoft MVP and global speaker at events like TED, Microsoft Build, and WeAreDevelopers, I focus on making complex tech accessible through content, community, and hands-on support. My mission is to connect, empower, and inspire developers to build impactful solutions.

speakers.name: Jordi Spranger
speakers.bio:
Jordi Spranger is an independent AI and robotics engineer based in Munich, bringing agentic AI to mobile robotics. He has delivered production-grade machine-learning solutions for large enterprises and built the intelligence layer for autonomous mobile robots. He is currently develop
ing spatial-memory systems for embodied agents on top of knowledge graphs, in line with his aspiring robotics startup for agentic robots.

talks.title: LLMs in the wild: Building an AI agent that survives production
talks.description:
Search works well when users know exactly what they're looking for. But travel discovery is rarely that simple. People express goals, preferences, budgets, and constraints in natural language.

At GetYourGuide, we set out to build a natural-language discovery experience that helps travelers find the right experiences from open-ended requests like "sunset tours in Barcelona for a couple under €50." Turning that vision into a production system required far more than adding an LLM on top of search.

In this talk, we'll share the journey from prototype to production and the key lessons we learned along the way. We'll discuss how AI systems can combine reasoning, retrieval, and personalization to better understand user intent, and what it takes to make those systems reliable at scale.

speakers.name: Giampaolo Casolla
speakers.bio: Giampaolo Casolla is a Senior Data Scientist at GetYourGuide in Berlin, working at the intersection of machine learning, generative AI, and product development. He builds AI-powered experiences used by travelers at scale, including GetYourGuide’s AI Discovery Agent in ChatGPT and AI Itineraries on Google Search. Previously at Amazon, his work on anomaly detection and forecasting contributed to more than $20M in cost savings. He holds an MSc in Applied Mathematics cum laude, has nine published papers with 380+ citations, and supports the local data community as Chair of the PyData Berlin Video Committee.

speakers.name: Steven Mi
speakers.bio:
Steven is a Software Engineer with 5+ years of experience building and productionizing machine learning systems that solve high-impact business problems. He has worked across domains including user acquisition, customer retention, content generation, supply optimization, and lead generation.

Currently at GetYourGuide, he is part of the Machine Learning and AI Platform team, where he focuses on enabling teams to independently build and operate production-grade LLM systems.

Outside of work, Steven co-organizes the AI in Production meetup in Berlin, a community dedicated to showcasing real-world AI applications across industries. In his free time, he enjoys exploring food and building tools he'd otherwise have to pay for.

talks.title: When Agents Meet Legacy: Never Change a Running System
talks.description:
I've spent a decade debugging undocumented C code, hand-written C++ Makefiles, and grown Java monoliths, knowing exactly which files will break production. Left "allowed to fail" CI/CD pipelines because fixing root causes is harder than ignoring them. I was curious: Can AI Agents help with modernization, and where would they still fail?

We'll live-code: untangling complex architectures in C and C++, and if Rust is the answer to everything, breaking Java monoliths to Kubernetes, where agents propose but humans validate, and fixing CI/CD burning budgets when culture resists tooling. The Tanuki IoT Platform environment presents more challenges when agents meet COBOL.

What I've learned: agents can't replace judgment on "should we change this?" You'll leave knowing where they help triage, where they fail on business context and experience, and which human strategies, like debugging, you still need. Agents are powerful guides, but the messy decisions are still yours.

speakers.name: Michael Friedrich
speakers.bio: Michael Friedrich is a Principal Developer Advocate at GitLab, focusing on production-ready Agentic AI use cases and DevSecOps efficiency. His journey from Hardware/Software Systems Engineering to DNS, monitoring, and GitLab trainings fuels his embedded homelab research on practical AI implementations. Michael educates at industry events through tutorials and live coding. When not traveling, he builds LEGO models and explores new tastes and cultures.

talks.title: Swapping Code, Losing Memory: A JVM Deep Dive
talks.description:
You’ve probably seen the option to hot swap code while debugging in your IDE, but have you ever wondered how it actually works under the hood? And more importantly, what could go wrong?
While stress testing an application that made heavy use of class reloading, I discovered a surprising issue: we were leaking memory and not just heap memory. This kicked off a deep dive into the internals of the JVM to understand what really happens when a class is reloaded.
In this talk, I’ll explain how I investigated the problem, what I learned about class representation in the JVM, and how code hot swapping really works in OpenJDK. You’ll leave with practical insights into debugging class reloading issues and a better understanding of what’s happening behind the scenes when your code changes on the fly.

speakers.name: Marco Sussitz
speakers.bio: Marco Sussitz is an engineer at Dynatrace who lives at the boundary of Java and C++. He writes JVMTI agents, instruments bytecode, and digs into JIT, memory, and thread behavior. You’ll often find him sorting out class loaders or, reading the spec longer than he should. Before Dynatrace, he worked on cloud video encoding with FFmpeg. Off hours he’s bouldering or in the mountains.

talks.title: Automated Security for the Entire SDLC
talks.description: TikTok's Global Security Organization (GSO) integrates AI into the engineering processes, helping catch security and compliance risks early—before they become expensive, slow, or customer-facing problems. In this session, we'll explore how GSO's AI-assisted security validation platform, SEVA, uses LLMs to continuously validate security controls across our SDLC, without slowing teams down. You'll learn how shifting security 'left' in the SDLC and taking care of vulnerability management early on in the process not only protects your products, but enables engineers to move faster.

speakers.name: Carey Liu
speakers.bio:
Carey Liu is a Product Security professional on TikTok's Global Security team, focusing on product security, AI-SDLC operations, and AI-native security governance. As part of the team, he is currently contributing to SEVA (Spec-driven Engineering Validation Agent), a product designed to bring security validation into product and technical design reviews earlier in the SDLC.

With 10 years of experience across security product operations, technical program management, and DevSecOps solution pre-sales, Carey is passionate about making security more scalable, actionable, and developer-friendly. His work focuses on shift-left security and emerging spec-driven AI coding workflow, helping engineering teams build securely by design before code is written.

Carey holds a Computer Science degree from the University of British Columbia and a Master’s degree in Information Security from UC Berkeley.

talks.title: Teaching an LLM to review code … like a Senior Engineer!
talks.description: There’s no doubt LLMs can generate plausible, working code – but can we trust them to review it? Being a helpful assistant is deeply ingrained in an LLM’s nature, but when it comes to code reviews, this works against us. What could have been a simple Pull Request approval turns into a lavish, flattering, one-page-long description of how great the code is, how extensive the test coverage is, and how brilliant the architectural choices are. No one has the time to read those reviews, and ultimately engineers stop paying attention. And even if the LLM does surface a real issue, chances are it’s going to be lost in the noise of dozens of good-to-haves and minor, irrelevant nitpicks. This is a story of how we built an LLM code review bot that behaves as a senior engineer – surfacing important, actionable violations of human-curated guidance and maximising signal-to-noise ratio.

speakers.name: Kesha Mykhailov
speakers.bio: Kesha is an engineer with over 20 years of experience in making customers happy through building product, running distributed systems, tuning socio-technical systems, and more recently building with AI. Kesha is a Principal Engineer at Intercom/Fin building the future of AI-centric customer service.

talks.title: Building Moduliths That Last: Patterns for Sustainable Module Integration
talks.description:
A system does not need to be distributed to have clean architectural boundaries. Moduliths (modular monoliths) have emerged as a popular alternative to microservices - But doesn't that mean we're going back to where we started from? Won't today's moduliths end up as Big Balls of Mud again in a few years?

The key to a sustainable modulith is clean integration between modules. The shared runtime offers more integration options but also creates the temptation to take shortcuts and create a hot mess. This talk compares different approaches to integrating modules in a modulith. We will explore how different domains suit specific patterns better than others, and distill that knowledge into practical heuristics. We will also examine tactics for establishing these patterns in existing codebases.

As a developer or architect, you will leave with a toolkit of modulith integration patterns and antipatterns, guidelines for choosing the right ones, and the knowledge to establish them in legacy applications.

speakers.name: Christoph Kober
speakers.bio:
Christoph is a passionate Software Crafter with a strong focus on software architecture and continuous learning.

In his role as Lead Software Engineer for Transformation at SQUER, he helps customers modernize their legacy applications, improve their software architecture, and reshape their software engineering culture.

He is convinced that principles and practices from the Domain-Driven Design universe are most helpful for tackling the complex challenges of large transformation initiatives.

talks.title: Your Code Is the Sales Team Now
talks.description: For decades the deal was simple: engineers build, sales sells. That deal just expired. Writing software has never been cheaper, yet selling it has never been more expensive. And a growing share of buyers aren't even human: AI agents now research, shortlist, and recommend products by reading your docs, your APIs, your error messages. This talk shows how distribution moved into the repository - why llms.txt, MCP servers, telemetry, and even a 403 error became revenue infrastructure - and what the fastest-growing AI-native companies like Lovable, Cursor, and n8n do differently. You'll leave with three things to ship next week. You're not writing features anymore.

speakers.name: Marcus König
speakers.bio: I’m Marcus, a growth operator and former VC. Over the past decade, I’ve worked with fast scaling B2B software and fintech companies to turn strong traction into repeatable, structured growth. Today, I partner with high-growth teams as a hands-on consultant, interim executive and advisor, aligning marketing, partnerships, sales and success. I focus on building sustainable, defensible go-to-market & engines, while driving commercial and product excellence.

talks.title: The Limits of LLMs in Real-World Applications
talks.description: Plenty of organizations have an AI strategy on paper; far fewer have it genuinely working. This panel is about closing that gap, with leaders who have moved from ambition to results. A practical conversation about making AI real across a business.

speakers.name: Deivids Vilkinsons
speakers.bio:
Dei is the CEO of HASH, the open-source platform for data integration and simulation. HASH develops ultra high-accuracy AI solutions for firms in safety-critical, error-sensitive, and regulated industries.

HASH has been developing "agentic" simulation tooling since 2019, when Dei established the firm with Joel Spolsky (the former founder of Stack Overflow, Trello, and Glitch). Today, HASH is profitable and has offices in New York, London, and Berlin.

Dei also leads one of the technical areas of the UK Advanced Research + Invention Agency's "Safeguarded AI" program, focused on developing high-trust interfaces for effective human-AI collaboration.

speakers.name: Guillaume Esnou
speakers.bio: Guillaume Esnou is Field CTO and Head of Technology for Invisible Technologies in EMEA, where he leads AI deployment strategy and technical delivery for enterprise clients. He brings deep expertise in AI and analytics, having built and scaled production-grade AI systems across sectors at McKinsey as an Associate Partner. Most recently, he led Engineering, Insights & Analytics at Surveyor Capital, Citadel hedge fund’s leading fundamental equities strategy. Guillaume holds an M.S. in Operations Research from Columbia University and a Diplôme d’Ingénieur in Mechanical and Industrial Engineering from Arts et Métiers. At Invisible, he focuses on building scalable AI systems that transform operations and drive measurable business impact.

speakers.name: Laura Moritz
speakers.bio:
Laura Moritz is a Tech Manager for Data & AI at Globant, where she leads AI and data programs for enterprise clients across industries including automotive, healthcare, finance, and education. With 10 years of consulting experience, she works at the intersection of AI strategy, data products, and implementation — from LLM-powered solutions and predictive models to data platforms and analytics.
Beyond her corporate work, Laura is engaged with Women in Tech, supporting initiatives that bring more women in technology onto stages and into leadership.

speakers.name: Mariam Hakobyan
speakers.bio: Mariam Hakobyan is the CEO and co-founder of Softr, the leading AI platform for building business apps without code. A former engineer turned entrepreneur, she has spent more than a decade building products and leading product and engineering teams, and is passionate about making software accessible to everyone.

talks.title: This App Reached 10,000 Users in One Week. Here's How.
talks.description:
One week before launch, this application didn't exist. Seven days later it was live, running in production, secured with enterprise authentication, deployed to the enterprise infrastructure, and being used by more than 10,000 employees world wide.

This session is about what happens when AI goes beyond helping developers write code—and starts acting as an entire software engineering team.

Using a real World Cup application built at Siemens as the case study, I'll walk through the complete journey from a simple business idea to a production-ready application. We'll look beyond code generation and explore how AI can drive discovery, requirements, architecture, implementation, testing, infrastructure, and deployment—while humans stay in control of the decisions that matter.

I'll also share the biggest lessons from recent visits to leading Silicon Valley companies and explain why the next generation of software engineering isn't about better prompts or faster coding. It's about orchestrating teams and AI on top of enterprise developer platforms.

If you've ever wondered what software engineering might look like in five years, this session will show you a production system - CREATE - at Siemens.

speakers.name: Mahran Meißner
speakers.position: Head of Technology and Innovation Space
speakers.bio: Mahran Meißner is Head of the Technology & Innovation Space at Siemens IT, where he focuses on turning emerging technologies into business value. His work spans AI agents, software engineering, humanoid robots, XR, and digital twins, with a strong emphasis on making advanced technologies accessible across the enterprise. He is the creator of CREATE, an AI platform that enables anyone to transform ideas into production-ready software. Mahran is a frequent speaker on enterprise AI, innovation, and the future of software development, sharing practical insights from building AI-powered products inside a global organization.

talks.title: Stop Renaming Teams, Start Product Thinking: A PM's Guide to Platform-as-a-Product
talks.description:
Everyone's talking about treating platforms as products. But when your platform team is drowning in tickets, firefighting upgrades, and struggling to prove ROI, "just apply product thinking" sounds like advice from someone who's never run a platform. And let's be honest: slapping a "Product Owner" title on someone and renaming your ops team won't magically fix anything.

So what does actually work? I've spent 5 years as a Platform Product Manager figuring that out. One example: transforming an internal monitoring platform from "universally avoided" to revenue-generating in 1.5 years—now serving 150+ Kubernetes clusters. The shift isn't magic. It starts with asking better questions about who your users really are, what value looks like, and how to prioritize when everything feels urgent.

In this talk, I'll share a framework that helped me make that shift—moving from thinking about technical components to understanding your actual platform users. You'll learn how to visualize what your platform really is and derive value metrics that prove impact beyond "uptime" and "tickets closed."

Whether you're a platform engineer curious about product thinking, or a team lead trying to escape the "internal service desk" trap, you'll leave with practical starting points to treat your platform as a product—for real.

speakers.name: Dominik Schmidle
speakers.bio: Dominik is a Group Product Manager for Platforms at Giant Swarm with the mission of simplifying developers' lives through intuitive developer platforms. He started as a Full Stack Software Engineer, discovered his passion for DevOps and product organizations, and transitioned into Product Management for cloud technology. He actively shares his experiences through talks, articles, and publications.

talks.title: Software That Fixes Itself
talks.description: What if your software could detect, diagnose, and someday even resolve its own issues — before a developer ever gets paged? In this fireside chat, Sentry CEO Milin Desai sits down with Rodrigue Schäfer, Vice President of Platform at Delivery Hero, to explore what "self-healing software" looks like in practice at one of the world's largest creative technology companies. The conversation will cover what self-healing means at Adobe's scale, how it reshapes the day-to-day reality for developers, and perhaps most importantly what engineers are able to focus on when software handles the routine for them. Part technical, part philosophical, this is a candid look at where software reliability is headed and what it means for the humans who build it.

speakers.name: Milin Desai
speakers.bio: Milin Desai currently serves as the CEO of Sentry. Used by more than 4 million developers and 150,000 organizations worldwide, Sentry helps every developer detect, understand, and fix broken code, fast. Milin joined Sentry from VMware where he helped build out multiple lines of business from networking (0->1b+) to multi cloud (0->100M+ SAAS). Earlier in his career, he held engineering and product roles at Veritas and Riverbed.

speakers.name: Rodrigue Schäfer
speakers.bio: With over two decades of experience at the forefront of the European tech scene in startup and scale-up environments, Rodrigue Schäfer focuses on driving innovation within Delivery Hero, one of the world’s leading local delivery platforms, by providing engineers with the tools and infrastructure they need to deliver high-quality products fast.

talks.title: Hacking MSSQL on Cloud. All of them. How I became sysadmin on Azure, AWS, GCP and Alibaba.
talks.description:
It started as a simple security research project on a local SQL Server instance. A single vulnerability led me down a rabbit hole — from compromising Azure SQL Database to successfully escalating privileges on GCP CloudSQL for SQL Server, Amazon RDS, and Alibaba ApsaraDB.

In this session, I’ll walk you through the techniques I used to escalate from a limited user to sysadmin on managed SQL Server platforms offered by the four biggest cloud providers. I’ll also demonstrate post-exploitation techniques, including how I retrieved plaintext [sa] passwords from internal logs and accessed highly sensitive internal metadata.

More importantly, I’ll share lessons on how these vulnerabilities were possible in the first place — and what you, as a developer, DBA, or security professional, can do to secure your applications against similar attack vectors.

Finally, I’ll share how each cloud provider responded to the vulnerabilities I disclosed, the remediation timelines, and the broader lessons this experience teaches us about cloud security.

speakers.name: Fabiano Amorim
speakers.bio:
Fabiano Amorim is a Microsoft Data Platform most valuable professional (MVP) since 2011. With over two decades of experience, Fabiano is well known in the database community for his performance tuning abilities and the many conference speaking engagements around the world.
He writes articles for Simple-Talk (https://www.simple-talk.com/author/fabiano-amorim/) and his blog is on http://blogfabiano.com.

talks.title: Instant KAI Sandboxes with vCluster: Multi-Tenant, Multi-Scheduler GPU Sharing
talks.description:
Kubernetes offers many ways to share GPUs, but a single, cluster-wide scheduler often forces trade-offs between utilization, stability, and team autonomy. This talk shows how vCluster makes the NVIDIA Kubernetes AI Scheduler (KAI) run as an opt-in service for each tenant—so platform teams can raise GPU density while keeping operations predictable.

What We’ll Cover

    Problem statement – why mixed workloads leave GPUs under-used and complicate on-call.
    vCluster fundamentals – lightweight control planes that isolate scheduling logic, not hardware.
    KAI at a glance – fractional GPU allocation, gang queues, topology awareness.
    Live demonstration – two vClusters on one host

Key Takeaways

    A reproducible pattern for running different schedulers side-by-side.
    Practical steps to increase GPU utilisation without adding more clusters.
    An isolation model that lets teams experiment safely.

speakers.name: Piotr Zaniewski
speakers.bio: An active contributor to open source, content creator on Medium and YouTube, focusing on practical, scalable solutions in cloud-native environments. DevOps and Platform Engineering practitioner and advocate.

talks.title: Teaching agents to pay: what devs need to know
talks.description:
With a global daily user base in the hundreds of millions, AI agents are rapidly becoming a primary interface for how people discover, evaluate, and purchase products. Enabling those products to be listed and paid for directly through agents opens an entirely new—and enormous—commerce channel. The Agent Commerce Protocol (ACP) and Shared Payment Tokens provide a secure framework for agent-driven commerce within Stripe’s ecosystem—without exposing payment data or sacrificing user control.
This session walks developers through the complete implementation: setting up Stripe integration, creating permission-based payment tokens, interacting with ACP endpoints, and designing trustworthy user experiences. You'll learn how to enable your agents to transact safely and predictably, handling everything from checkout flows to error scenarios and webhook events.

speakers.name: Benjamin Smith
speakers.bio: A Developer Relations leader with 15+ years of experience driving global adoption of cloud and fintech platforms. With roles at AWS, Stripe, and Broadcom, I’ve built scalable developer engagement engines, shaped compelling product narratives, and launched hands-on programs that turn complex technology into real business impact. Known for high-energy keynotes, strategic program design, and cross-functional leadership, I bridge developers, product teams, and executives to accelerate innovation and deliver results.

talks.title: Debugging Humans: How MBTI Helps Engineering Teams Communicate Better
talks.description:
Software teams spend enormous effort on codes - yet many of the biggest productivity issues are not technical at all. They come from miscommunication, mismatched expectations, and avoidable friction between equally capable engineers.

In this talk, I will explore how MBTI - a 16 personality assessment - can be used as a practical communication framework for engineer teams - not as a personality label or hiring tool, but as a shared language to understand different working and communication preferences.

I will share how small adjustments in communication can dramatically improve team effectiveness.

This session focuses on actionable, engineer-friendly techniques to reduce friction, improve collaboration, and build high-performing teams.

speakers.name: Hazel Wat
speakers.bio:
Hazel is an experienced Analyst & Consultant with a strong track record of bridging technology, data and business needs. Currently with Schwarz Digits , an in-house technology powerhouse for Lidl & Kaufland supermarkets.

Born & raised in Hong Kong, studied & lived in USA for 15 years; currently residing in Germany for 11 years. Lived and worked globally, bringing a multicultural perspective to engineering soft skills and team dynamics.

Hazel is passionate about improving team communication and performance, bridging the communication gap between technical and business colleagues.

talks.title: From APIs to MCP: Enterprise Governance, Registry, and Controls
talks.description:
APIs remain the foundation of enterprise integration, but AI agents are changing how capabilities are discovered and consumed. MCP standardizes tool discovery and invocation, enabling agents to interact with enterprise systems through reusable tools. The challenge is not enabling MCP. The challenge is governing it at scale.

In this talk, we will discuss how to operationalize MCP in an enterprise by leveraging existing API Management capabilities instead of creating a parallel governance stack. We will cover how to build a shared registry for APIs and MCP servers that acts as the discovery layer for modern agents, and we will walk through the governance controls that matter in practice.

Attendees will leave with a practical blueprint for implementing MCP safely and repeatably at enterprise scale, making MCP adoption scalable, observable, and compliant.

speakers.name: Stefan Mesquita
speakers.bio: Stefan Mesquita leads the Platform Experience team for Corporate Bank platforms at Deutsche Bank. He is responsible for scaling the bank’s core API, Kafka, and BigQuery infrastructure to drive organizational efficiency. With over 15 years of experience in the financial sector, Stefan specializes in Platform Engineering and defining the architectural patterns that allow product teams to deliver faster. By decoupling infrastructure complexity from product development, he enables the organization to focus on business value and innovation. Stefan is a strategic leader dedicated to bridging the gap between large-scale systems engineering and digital business strategy.

talks.title: The LLM Evolution: From Sequence Imitation to Verifiable Reasoning
talks.description:
For the last decade, the recipe for AI was simple: more data, bigger models. By feeding neural networks the entire internet, we taught them to imitate human language with startling accuracy. But as we exhaust the world's high-quality text data, a new question arises: How do we scale intelligence when there is nothing left to imitate?

In this talk, we trace the evolution of Language Modeling — from counting words with n-grams, through Word2Vec and the Transformer, to the reasoning paradigm sparked by OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek R1. This "Data Wall" is real — but it ends imitation, not progress: the industry is pivoting from System 1 (fast imitation) to System 2 (deliberate reasoning), opening test-time compute as a second scaling axis where models "think" before they answer.

Following the AlphaGo Zero precedent, we'll see how reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards lets models keep improving without new human data, and how coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor point that same propose–verify loop at your codebase. Along the way, Verifier's Law and the  "jagged edge" of intelligence will tell us which tasks AI will master next — and which it won't.

This session is for any developer who wants to understand where this is heading — and how our role evolves from writing syntax to architecting the specs, tests, and feedback loops that guide AI reasoning.

speakers.name: Kamen Petroff
speakers.bio: Software Developer at cycos AG (an Atos company) since 2001, specializing in real-time media streaming, web conferencing, and IVR solutions. Shifted focus to Applied AI in 2017, working on research projects in the fields of Natural Language Processing and Deep Learning. Creator of `kpe/bert-for-tf2`, one of the pioneering implementations of the Transformer architecture for TensorFlow 2, dedicated to bridging the gap between cutting-edge AI research and practical software engineering.

talks.title: User 1st! Technology 2nd! Stop building AI nobody uses - start delivering real business outcomes
talks.description:
Most products and solutions don’t fail because of missing technology — they fail because users show up too late.

Organizations invest heavily in AI, platforms, and architectures, yet still struggle to create impact. While more than 80% of developers already use or plan to use AI tools, holistic, user-driven approaches across different personas remain the exception rather than the rule.

The real problem is not at a single stage. It starts in ideation, gets diluted in requirements, disappears in architecture decisions, and becomes expensive in testing, operations, and later optimization. If users do not actively shape the value chain end to end, organizations don’t just build the wrong features — they scale the wrong outcomes.

In this session, we show how to put the user back where value is actually created: across the full lifecycle — from ideation and requirements engineering through rapid prototyping, development, testing, operations, and continuous optimization.

We also show why this takes more than one shiny model or a preferred platform: it requires technology-agnostic thinking, end-to-end delivery discipline, built-in quality and compliance, governance and security, and the ability to scale solutions across markets under the respective regulatory standards.

You will learn how to turn AI-augmented engineering from a promising idea into solutions users adopt, businesses trust, and organizations can scale in the real world.

speakers.name: Mateusz Gren
speakers.bio:
Mateusz Gren is Head of Software Development at Atos in Austria, where he leads large-scale software and AI initiatives with teams of several hundred engineers. With a background in Business Informatics and more than a decade of hands-on experience as a software architect, developer, and engineering leader, he operates at the intersection of architecture, execution, and business impact.

Beyond enterprise systems, he actively builds and operates his own AI-assisted applications using modern web stacks, applying production-grade thinking to personal productivity systems - building and evolving personal software systems for sports performance, finance, and decision-making using generative AI and minimal code. His talks focus on what actually works, what breaks, and how developers can stay in control while leveraging AI as a genuine multiplier rather than a buzzword.

speakers.name: Peter Hock
speakers.bio:
Peter Hock is Head of Digital Applications for Germany, Austria, Czechia and Poland. As a senior executive in digital applications and software-driven transformation, he brings more than 20 years of experience in IT services and consulting—on both the customer and provider side—and across international business environments.

He leads global delivery teams across on-, near-, and offshore and helps organizations design, build, and operate business-critical digital solutions end to end.

His focus is not on technology for its own sake, but on how organizations translate strategy into execution and measurable outcomes. He specializes in structuring complex initiatives across the full lifecycle—from idea and requirements to delivery, operation, and continuous optimization.

Peter is particularly driven by challenging implementations—where complexity, scale, and real-world constraints demand clear ownership, strong governance, and tight alignment between business, users, and engineering.

------------

Mateusz Gren is Head of Software Development at Atos in Austria and a driving force behind large-scale digital transformation in enterprise environments. Starting his career as a software developer, he brings a hands-on perspective to leading complex programs that combine modern software engineering, DevOps, and AI.

In recent years, Mateusz has been at the forefront of integrating generative AI into software development - from code generation and automated testing to new collaboration models between engineers and AI systems. His focus is not on hype, but on making AI work in real-world enterprise projects with strict requirements for governance, quality, and scalability.

As a speaker, he shares practical insights on how organizations can adopt AI in software engineering without losing control. His perspective bridges technology, delivery, and leadership - with one goal: building better software, faster.

talks.title: Native Speed, Java Comfort: Calling Rust from the JVM with Project Panama
talks.description:
The JVM is one of the most impressive pieces of software engineering, making Java incredibly fast for most workloads. But sometimes, "fast" isn't enough. For domains like scientific computing, AI, or processing massive volumes of text, we need to call highly-optimized native libraries written in C++ or Rust to gain a critical performance edge or access functionality not available on the JVM. For decades, this meant using the Java Native Interface (JNI)—a powerful but notoriously complex and unsafe bridge to the native world.

Enter Project Panama. With the Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API, Java finally has a safe, supported, and elegant way to call native code, eliminating the need for brittle glue code and manual memory management. This talk puts it to the test with a classic Java challenge: the regular expression engine.

Join me for a practical, hands-on session where we will replace Java's capable but often-outperformed regex engine with Rust's highly optimized regex crate. We will walk through two implementations side-by-side: the "old way" with JNI and the "new way" with Project Panama. You will see firsthand how Panama simplifies interfacing with native code and improves safety. We'll cap it off with live benchmarks to compare the performance of both approaches against standard Java regex, helping you understand not just how to call native code, but also when it's truly worth the effort.

speakers.name: Gonzalo Ortiz Jaureguizar
speakers.bio: I am a software engineer specialized in developing databases in Java. I love understanding how libraries and frameworks work under the hood and to design and implement high-performance systems. I have worked on prototypes such as ToroDB, the first Spanish database unicorn Devo and since 2022 I'm working at StarTree as an Apache Pinot contributor.

talks.title: AI Driven Development
talks.description: In software development, AI has evolved from a better stack overflow to a powerful co-pilot that is already making things possible today that we could only dream of five years ago. After more than 50 customer projects involving AI, David Tielke will show in this session which tools really add value, how they can be used profitably for everyone in development, and where the limits currently lie.

speakers.name: David Tielke
speakers.bio: David Tielke is a consultant, coach, and trainer with over 15 years of experience in high-level software development. His expertise focuses on software quality, software architecture, and agile development processes. Having trained more than 30,000 participants, delivered over 150 presentations at renowned conferences, and published numerous articles in industry magazines, he has shared his knowledge and expertise widely. On his YouTube channel, he shares his passion for software development and provides practical insights into current industry topics.

talks.title: Vertical Slice Architecture: Micro Frontends Across Mobile, Backend & ML
talks.description:
Micro frontends are often discussed in the context of web applications. But what if we extend the idea beyond UI - into mobile, backend services, and machine learning?

In this talk, I’ll present a vertical slice architecture where each feature team owns everything required to deliver business value:
- Android UI
- Kotlin Multiplatform shared domain logic
- Kotlin backend service
- Python-based ML model
- API contracts

Instead of organizing codebases by technical layers, we organize by business features. This reduces coordination overhead, increases deployment independence, and aligns teams with product outcomes.

speakers.name: Jens Posingies
speakers.bio:
Jens Posingies is an Engineering Manager at Redcare Pharmacy with 25 years of experience in software development, architecture and engineering leadership. Born and raised in East Germany, he studied Business Information Systems at the University of Lüneburg and Media & Education at the University of Rostock.

Over his career, Jens has worked in roles ranging from Java and Node.js developer to Solution Architect and Engineering Manager, including positions at Zalando, TUI, HRS and Redcare Pharmacy. His current focus is on lateral leadership, end-to-end ownership and modular software architectures such as microservices, microfrontends and Kotlin Multiplatform.

He is also a certified nerd with deep expertise in Back to the Future and Star Trek.

speakers.name: Robert Pazurek
speakers.bio:
I'm developing Software for over 20 years now. I've worked at different companies from small 10 men startups up to huge enterprises operating world wide both freelance and as an employee.
For a while I ran my own small personal fitness training studio and dabbled in many side projects that had nothing to do with software development but focused on communication and working with people.

Over time I acquired a lot of experience and knowledge regarding learning and skill development. Be it as a personal trainer, father to two kids (and one dog) or husband to a great agile coach and systemic organizational developer. How people learn and how systems evolve and develop in positive ways has become a passion topic of mine.

speakers.name: Vivek Kuppenhalli
speakers.bio:
I am a Staff Engineer in the Mobile team at Redcare Pharmacy, specializing in Android application development and large-scale architecture design. I lead architectural transformations that enable teams to adopt multi-module strategies and take ownership of domain-driven development within a shared codebase.

I advocate clean architectural patterns that improve scalability, build performance, and team autonomy. Recently, I have been exploring a feature-driven “micro frontend” approach across mobile and backend systems, leveraging Kotlin Multiplatform to share business logic while preserving native UI independence on Android and iOS.

talks.title: Fighting the Next Wave of Cybercrime
